Sutton told the council that while he did not oppose the scheme “as such”, it was “counterintuitive” to accept the club’s claims that the site would benefit the local environment as about 40% of the park would be lost.

“In my opinion, if the council were to accept this, their decision could be easily challenged,” he added.

But Wigley said council officers had said in a planning report for councillors that there was “no objection to the proposed development”, despite Sutton telling the authority that this did not reflect his advice.

She continued that Sutton’s report “clearly informed the planning officers’ views” on the environmental impact of the scheme and should have been presented as a “background document”, meaning members of the public could have inspected it.

Wigley said: “[The law] does not permit this kind of salami slicing, where a planning officer can disclose parts of a report they agree with but can avoid public scrutiny of the parts of the report they do not agree with.”

James Maurici KC, representing Spurs, said Sutton’s views were “no more than an assertion” and that Guardians of Whitewebbs had “failed to provide any evidence” that it had been prejudiced by the council’s failure to provide the document.

He continued: “It is highly likely, indeed inevitable, given the absence of any evidence of prejudice, that the outcome for the claimant would not have been substantially different if the conduct complained of had not occurred.”

But Kerr said the council’s noncompliance with rules was “serious” and that councillors were “materially misled” by the exclusion of Sutton’s report.

Alessandro Georgiou, the Conservative leader of Enfield council since May 2026, said the authority was delighted with the decision and that it withdrew its defence as it would “not have been in the best interests of residents across the borough”.

He added: “We said we would protect Whitewebbs Park from this unacceptable proposal and we will now move forward with plans that reflect the needs of the local community and also preserve and protect this important area of Enfield.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino requested to appear before House Committee over Donald Trump relationship after World Cup chaos
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino requested to appear before House Committee over Donald Trump relationship after World Cup chaos

A leading Democratic US lawmaker has written to Gianni Infantino to ask him to appear before the House Judiciary Committee.

Rep. Jamie Raskin, the ranking member on the House Committee, has requested that the FIFA chief be scrutinised over his relationship with president Donald Trump.

4 Infantino has been requested to appear in front of the committee as his relationship with Trump is called into question Credit: Getty

During the 2026 World Cup this summer, questions were raised around Infantino and Trump amid multiple controversies.

The US president admitted that he had called the FIFA boss to overturn Folarin Balogun's suspension for their last-16 game.

FIFA then went on to announce Balogun was free to play against Belgium for the USA, with his ban suspended following an shock change of protocol.

That decision caused major backlash, and Infantino and FIFA were slammed, being accused of bending to Trump's wishes.

On top of that, even before the World Cup, Infantino handed Trump the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize, while FIFA have used office space in Trump Tower in New York City.

Infantino and Trump relationship questioned

Now, due to those actions, Rep. Raskin is pushing FIFA to provide all records on its contact with President Trump by August 9.

A letter was sent on Sunday night and seen by The Athletic, who report that Raskin has requested Infantino to provide 'a list of anything of value (including transfer of money, gifts, prizes, awards, or public appearances) given to President Trump, members of his Administration, or their family members, or any entity associated with them, such as The Trump Organization.'

It has also been requested that Infantino and FIFA provide visitor logs for FIFA’s Miami and New York City offices.

Raskin wrote that his letter 'serves as notice' for all communications to be preserved 'between FIFA personnel and individuals affiliated with the Trump Administration or its inaugural committee — including disappearing messages exchanged on ephemeral communication platforms, such as Signal, Telegram, WhatsApp, X, and Truth Social.'

And at the end of the letter, Raskin asks that Infantino appears for an interview with the House Judiciary Committee, questioning whether the relationship between FIFA and Trump has gone too far.

4 Rep. Raskin has asked for records of communications between FIFA and the Trump Administration Credit: Getty

Raskin also requests all FIFA documents and communications since 2024 with any US official, or anyone associated with the presidential transition before Trump returned to power.

He also claims that FIFA's office space on the 17th floor of Trump Tower in Manhattan might ordinarily retail for $600,000 per year.

And the letter reportedly reads: “These actions appear designed to induce President Trump and his Administration to make decisions in FIFA’s favour."

As well as that, Raskin calls FIFA's controversial ticketing policy into question, with fans complaining over misleading ticket locations, variable pricing and 'higher-tiered' tickets.

“FIFA has taken its newfound favored status in the Trump Administration as a sign that it may rip off its consumers, most notably, by employing illegal price gouging and fraudulent sales tactics for the World Cup," the letter is said to have read.

“FIFA also introduced dynamic pricing, leading to sharply higher prices for many games. Even once a fan buys a ticket, FIFA may, at its own discretion, move them into a worse seat in a worse section. This is plainly unlawful, anti-consumer conduct … But President Trump’s DOJ and Federal Trade Commission have sat idly by, doing nothing.”

4 A White House spokeman has responded to the request from Raskin Credit: AFP

Raskin is unlikely to have the power to force Infantino to appear in front of the House Judiciary Committee as Democrats have the house minority - but it they take it back in November, further scrutiny could be coming the way of the FIFA president.

White House spokesman responds

The Athletic have also revealed a response from White House spokesman Davis Ingle in their report.

“Lightweight Jamie Raskin (is) a stupid person’s idea of a smart person," Ingle said. “No other president in history could have pulled off the historic feat that President Trump delivered for the American people and the world.

“Thanks to his bold vision and decisive leadership, the 2026 FIFA World Cup generated billions of dollars in revenue, created a massive economic boost across host cities, and delivered a safe, secure, and seamless experience for millions of fans and athletes from around the globe.

"It will undoubtedly go down as one of the greatest and most successful sporting events in history.”

Infantino statement

The call for Infantino to appear before the House Judiciary Committee comes after he hit back at FIFA's critics.

4 FIFA chief Infantino had already released a statement slamming his critics Credit: Getty

He launched a scathing attack on Instagram, writing: "To all of you who missed watching kids, babies, grandparents, and parents come together for the beautiful game, I say sorry that the matches are now over and sorry that you missed all that joy and togetherness.

"Sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all.

"To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering the best show in the world.

"While you hide, we are exploring the streets of Canada, Mexico, and the United States, talking with fans, engaging with people and ensuring everyone's safety.

"While you divide, we unite."

Infantino suggested the World Cup experienced 'no violence, no incidents, 100 per cent safety and security, only joy and happiness'.

And he also claimed seven million people from more than 200 countries attended matches this summer.

Sports.title: Premier League and EFL begin immediate trial on rule change to combat dark arts
Sports.content:
Premier League and EFL begin immediate trial on rule change to combat dark arts

A new rule will be trialled in English football this season in a bid to clamp down on goalkeeper tactical timeouts.

The controversial issue drew criticism from managers, fans and pundits throughout the previous campaign.



2 A goalkeeper receiving treatment will affect his teammates who play outfield from August Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Goalkeepers will no longer be able to go down to receive treatment without a player leaving the field of play under the new rule.

It follows an agreement with the FA which will see the Premier League, Football League, National League and Women’s Super League trial the rule change this season.

The International Football Association Board (IFAB) have granted permission for the trial to take place.



Rule change trial

From the start of the season, teams must remove an outfield player when their goalkeeper receives on-field treatment.

Managers will have ten seconds to select a player to leave the pitch once the referee has signalled for the physio to come on.



If they do not nominate a player within ten seconds, the captain will automatically be chosen to leave the field.

The new rule will be trialled for the first time on Saturday during the Carabao Cup preliminary round tie involving Tranmere and Rochdale.



It is understood a variation of the rule will also be used in Australia's A-League this term.

However, their implementation of the rule will see the captain always having to leave the field.

FIFA also clamped down on the potential breaks in play during this summer's World Cup.

2 This trial should lead to fewer instances of goalkeepers receiving treatment from physios Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



Players were not permitted to go to the touchline when goalkeepers were receiving treatment, instead gathering in the centre circle.

Controversial timeouts

This season's trial follows a rise in goalkeepers being perceived to fake injuries in order to force stoppages in play for unnecessary treatment last season.

Their teammates would then be able to receive instructions from the manager and coaching staff on the touchline.

Leeds United boss Daniel Farke publicly accused Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma of faking an injury in November.



His outburst followed City's 3-2 Premier League win over Leeds at the Etihad Stadium.

Speaking after the match, Farke exclaimed: "Everyone knows why he went down.

"It is not the elephant in the room. Why he went down it was obvious. It is within the rules. It is smart.

"If I like it? If it's within the sense of fair play? If it should be like this I will keep to myself. It is up to the authorities to find a solution.



"I ask the fourth official at this point if you want to do something. Our hands are tied.

"If we don't educate our players in football what to do in terms of fair play and sportsmanship and whatever and if we just try to bend the rules and even do a fake injury in order to do an additional team talk, it is not what I like personally. But if it is within the rules I can't complain."

Sports.title: James Trafford closes in on record transfer to new Premier League club after Newcastle interest
Sports.content:
James Trafford closes in on record transfer to new Premier League club after Newcastle interest

Leeds United are close to agreeing a deal to sign Manchester City goalkeeper James Trafford, talkSPORT understands.

Trafford has been keen to leave City this summer in search of a No.1 role at another Premier League club.



3 Trafford won two trophies in his first season with Man City Credit: Getty

The 23-year-old had indicated that he wants to join Leeds and he is set to become their highest-paid player.

Negotiations have been moving quickly and so much so that a deal for Trafford is now close to being agreed.

talkSPORT understands that Leeds will pay a club-record £40million plus bonuses for the wantaway England international.



Trafford joined the Etihad side last summer in a £27m deal from Burnley - just two years after City sold him for £14m.

He started in the opening three Premier League games of the season, before he was left blindsided by City's deadline-day swoop to sign Gianluigi Donnarumma.



Trafford ended up playing just four times under Pep Guardiola in the league, but a further 13 games in cup competitions.

Man City won both the FA Cup and Carabao Cup last season.

Trafford heading for Leeds

Leeds have seen Illan Meslier and Karl Darlow depart this summer, to back-up roles at Arsenal and Man United respectively.



Lucas Perri joined the club last summer and made 15 Premier League appearances last season, but Daniel Farke will sign a new No.1.

And it seems Trafford is going to be his man, with the deal expected to be finalised this week between Leeds and Man City.

3 Trafford is set to be Farke's new No.1 at Elland Road Credit: Getty

Newcastle have held a long-term interest in the goalkeeper too, but have recently signed 20-year-old Ewen Jaouen.



Nick Pope remains on the books too, while Aaron Ramsdale returned to Southampton after his loan spell.

The Magpies have not held any recent talks or placed a bid.

The last conversations occurred when Trafford was discussed as an option when Man City explored signing Sandro Tonali.

Trafford blindsided

Leeds-bound Trafford initially joined City last summer with the full expectation of being their No.1 for the season.

But commenting on Donnarumma's transfer, he has revealed he wasn't told the club would be signing the Euro 2020 winner.



3 Donnarumma was signed by City on deadline day for £26m Credit: Getty

He said: "I didn't expect the situation to happen, but it happened, so just get on with it. It’s happened so I work very hard every day and see what happens, give it my best shot."

Trafford added: "No, it wasn't that, but it [the plan] wasn't what happened. It is what it is. It's football, it is what it is, you've got to keep grafting every day and the games that come, play as hard as you can.

"It's just another experience to add to my career and yeah, it has been good learning.



"Let’s take it a day at a time and try and work as hard as I can and whatever happens, happens.

"I’ve obviously got a contract, so don’t know what happens next season. I just know that I’ll just take it a day at a time and try and improve.”

Man City start their Premier League campaign against Bournemouth, while Leeds travel to Nottingham Forest on the opening day.

Sports.title: Ex-Manchester United striker Chicharito signs for club that has never played a game
Sports.content:
Ex-Manchester United striker Chicharito signs for club that has never played a game

Former Manchester United striker Javier Hernandez has signed for American club Atletico Dallas, who have never played a game.

Atletico Dallas were only founded in November 2024 and are a brand new expansion side set to join the USL Championship.



4 Ex-Man United star Hernandez has joined Atletico Dallas, who have never played a game Credit: Getty

Ahead of the 2027 season, the second tier of the United States football ladder is adding one extra club to its league.

There are also four new teams joining the USL (United Soccer League) League One at the start of the new campaign.

The Dallas outfit will be competing in the Championship and preparations are being ramped up for their maiden game.



Player and staff recruitment only started this year, with plans in place to hold trials to find people suitable to join the club.

Man United pre-season on MUTV Fans can watch Michael Carrick prepare for the new season and how the squad is shaping up across Finland, Norway, Sweden and Ireland. MUTV is the home of all Manchester United pre-season fixtures. It’s the opportunity to watch new faces, young players, returning names, tactical clues and the first signs of what United might become over the next season. MUTV on Sky: £7 extra a month. Existing Sky TV customers only. 31 day rolling contract. Cancel anytime with 31 days’ notice. Requires compatible Sky Q or Sky Stream boxes.

But they won't need a try-out for their first transfer in the club's history, as they're bringing in a name that is known worldwide.



Hernandez, also known as Chicharito, has signed for Atletico Dallas.

The 38-year-old has become their first and only player, starting his career at the club by helping contribute to their project.

He won't make his full debut in Texas until March 2027, when the USL Championship season starts, leaving him with eight months to watch the team get built around him.



4 Hernandez is a Mexico legend and will be playing in Texas, which has a strong connection to his home nation Credit: Getty

Chicharito has not played for a club since his contract with Mexican side Guadalajara expired in December last year.

But the ex-Man United and Real Madrid striker will now continue his career by taking a unique opportunity.

'I didn't come here to finish my career'

Speaking after his arrival at Atletico Dallas was confirmed, he said: “I've been fortunate to live the dreams that every young footballer hopes to experience. I've worn some of the biggest shirts in the world and played in incredible stadiums in front of passionate supporters.



"Opportunities like this, though, are different.”

Hernandez added: “I believe Dallas deserves a club that reflects its passion for football, its diversity, and its future. I want to help create a winning culture, inspire young players across North Texas, and give our supporters a team they can believe in from the very beginning.

"I didn't come here simply to finish my career. I came here to help build the future of football in Dallas.”

4 Chicharito scored 59 goals for Man United across his five-year-spell at the club Credit: Getty - Contributor

Chicharito's history-making move

As mentioned, Chicharito left Guadalajara at the end of 2025, after taking his club appearances to 121 following a second stint.



Before that, he played in the MLS with LA Galaxy, so he will have experience of the football pyramid in the USA.

Hernandez headed to LA in 2020 from Sevilla, whom he signed for when leaving West Ham and the Premier League.

He spent two years with the Hammers, scoring 17 goals in 63 games in all competitions, having joined from Bayer Leverkusen.

The forward played the most games in his career for Man United though, featuring 157 times and scoring 59 goals in five years.



On top of his club career, Chicharito also remains Mexico's all-time top goalscorer, seven years after international retirement.

4 Hernandez (middle) spent his summer working as a World Cup pundit in the States Credit: Getty

He netted 52 goals in 109 caps for his country from 2009 to 2019.

Now, Hernandez takes a unique step towards the end of his playing days, signing for Atletico Dallas in a historic transfer.

His latest move comes after he worked as a pundit during the 2026 World Cup in the United States this summer.

Sports.title: Tara Kirk leaves Peterborough United to join rival club in same division
Sports.content:
Tara Kirk has left Peterborough United Women to sign for rivals West Bromwich Albion Women.

Kirk, who has become a viral sensation on social media after some impressive form in 2023, spent four years with Posh.

2 Kirk (far left) has departed Peterborough after scoring 55 goals in 96 games Credit: Instagram @taramaekirk

The striker joined the Women's National League North side in 2021, but she has now departed to sign for West Brom.

The Baggies are in the same division as her now-former club, who were promoted to the third tier last season.

Kirk scored 55 goals in 96 games in all competitions for Peterborough, starring on the pitch and building a huge following online.

She has also made appearances for the Republic of Ireland's youth side, whilst starting her career with Leicester City.

Speaking following her move to West Brom, the 23-year-old forward said: "I’m so excited. It’s nice to get it over the line.

"I can’t wait to get started. Everyone has been so welcoming.

"I'm very fortunate with the way I’ve been accepted in the group, and I can't wait to do as well as I can for the club.

“I’m very impressed with the facilities. It’s really great that the women’s team get looked after so well here, and that was a big deal for me when joining.

“I’ve spoken with Siobhan Hodgetts-Still [head coach] and Martyn Irvine [interim head coach].

"They’ve both been super welcoming and it’s been great to meet them and train under them. They’re both very ambitious and that matches me perfectly.”

Saying goodbye

Kirk boasted an incredible record at Peterborough, and after achieving promotion last season, she's sad to depart.

The forward posted on social media after her exit was confirmed: "Posh, I wasn’t just at a football club, I was a part of a family for the past four years where I made many achievements as well as always wanting to get Peterborough United promoted.

"Football is all about new challenges, new experiences, new opportunities and so it’s time to move on.

"Posh fans, you have made me feel so so grateful and I thank you all for your incredible continued support throughout the years, I mean that with my whole heart. I am very lucky to have had you.

"My teammates, the staff and the club, I thank you for the best memories on and off the pitch, and will always carry them with me."

Peterborough Women's manager Jake Poole has also spoken about the departure of one of his stars in Kirk, saying: "Tara has played a massive part in the growth and success of Peterborough United Women.

2 Kirk played for Posh for four years, but she's now joined a rival in West Brom Credit: Getty

"We are grateful for her contribution, not just on the pitch, but as a terrific team-mate and person to have within the squad.

"We wish her all the best in her new challenge and I have no doubt she will add value to a squad wherever she goes in the future."

Sports.title: ‘Great bitterness’ – Andrea Pirlo being denied Italy job sparks shock double resignation
Sports.content:
Paolo Maldini has quit as technical director of the Italian Football Federation after Andrea Pirlo was not appointed head coach.

The federation's president, Giovanni Malago, opted not to appoint Pirlo due to his commercial ties to a Russian betting company.

5 Maldini and Leonardo have left their jobs just 16 days after being appointed due to the Pirlo drama Credit: Getty

5 Pirlo had been removed from the running for the Italy job due to commercial ties with Russia Credit: Fonbet

Pirlo had emerged as the leading candidate to succeed Gennaro Gattuso after former Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola turned down the post.

The AC Milan icon, who was part of the last Azzurri side to lift the World Cup as a player in 2006, had strong support from the newly-appointed Maldini and his adviser Leonardo.

But the fallout from Pirlo's role as a global ambassador for Russia's largest bookmaker, Fonbet, led to political resistance.

And, according to Sky Italy, the decision not to name the Italy legend as boss has led to Maldini and Leonardo stepping down.

Maldini was only given the role as technical director 16 days ago.

Pirlo will not be Italy's new head coach

“Out of respect for the institutions, the federation and everybody involved, I have chosen to remain silent until now,” Pirlo wrote in a statement, confirming he won't be Italy boss on Instagram.

“However, after learning last night that I am no longer a candidate for the Italy national team head coach position, I feel it is necessary to clarify a few points.

“Over the past few days, I have watched with great bitterness as the debate regarding my name and the possibility of my taking on the role of Italy national team head coach unfolded.

“Throughout my career, first as a player and then as a coach, I have always performed my duties with full respect of the laws of the countries I have worked in and the contracts I signed.

“The professional collaboration that is the subject of recent controversy came about as part of my working experience in the United Arab Emirates and is exclusively of a commercial and sporting nature. Attributing political meaning to this collaboration means attributing convictions to me that I have never expressed and that I do not hold.

5 Former Italy captain Pirlo made over 100 appearances for his country Credit: AFP

“I wish to thank Maldini and Leonardo for the respect and faith that they showed in me. I know their competence, their seriousness, and the love that they have always dedicated to Italian football.

“However, it is regrettable that a decision based on sporting grounds was quickly dragged into a public debate that ended up attributing motives and intentions to my name that never existed.

"My love for Italy does not depend on a job. It is part of my history, my identity, and will continue to accompany me, always.”

Why did Guardiola reject Italy?

Guardiola was the first-choice candidate to succeed Gattuso, who left his post in March after Italy failed to qualify for a third successive World Cup.

Italian football expert Daniele Fisichella explained on the latest talkSPORT episode of Danny Kelly's Trans Euro Express podcast: “The name of Guardiola has been invented, has been named since May.

“Basically, the Italian FA, with the newly appointed Paolo Maldini, the former player, as a managing director, and Leonardo [Araujo], the Brazilian, as an adviser, they tried to get the best manager available on the market, which is Pep Guardiola, they met in Barcelona last Saturday, hours before the World Cup final, to explain the proposal and the idea of him managing not only the first team, but also be in charge of the restructuring of the Italian football.

5 Pep Guardiola bid farewell to Manchester City in May after a decade at the club Credit: Getty

“Of course, a fascinating proposal, albeit for the fact that there is quite a lot of work to do in the Italian FA and in the Italian national team.

“Guardiola was honoured; he said, but very politely replied, thanks, but no thanks, for different reasons.

“Also because he wants to take a step down for a bit from football, for personal reasons, for family reasons,” Fisichella continued.

“So even the idea of living in Barcelona and almost working remotely and then going to Italy to manage the team every three or four months didn't quite appeal to him.”

Who did Italy try to hire next?

Fisichella continued: “So then the Italian FA tried to convince Carlo Ancelotti, via Paolo Maldini, of course, his former teammate and former player at AC Milan. But Carlo Ancelotti had already committed to stay at Brazil.

“So the first choice, really the only viable choice, remained Andrea Pirlo, who, by the way, is a great friend of Paolo Maldini, having played together at AC Milan.

5 Pirlo was named a global brand ambassador for Fonbet in October 2025 Credit: Getty

“And Paolo Maldini has always been a big sponsor of Andrea Pirlo. Why? Because Andrea Pirlo is considered almost somebody who has also got this aura.

“He was a fantastic player, but he's considered somebody who is destined to be a great manager.

“Unfortunately, his CV and his career doesn't quite tell the same story. His first ever coaching experience was at Juventus in 2021, and he didn't do really well there. They finished second; they won the cup.

“But that team never really convinced and was never able to impose themselves, despite still having Cristiano Ronaldo in very good form as well.

“Then he went to manage Sampdoria in the second division, got sacked after a year and a half, then went to Turkey and managed to finish fourth with a team outside of the top three anyway.

“And last year was managing in Dubai's second division, which, by the way, he won the championship there. So at least he got United FC promoted to the first division.”

Pirlo's ties to Russian betting company

Regardless of his less-than-glittering managerial CV, Pirlo looked set to become 'the new Italian manager on a very cheap contract'.

“Only 1.5 million euros [£1.2m], compared, for example, to [Jurgen] Klopp, who earns 7-8m at Germany,” Fisichella added on talkSPORT on Sunday evening. “So he's obviously much, much cheaper.

“However, it has emerged that Pirlo earlier this year in May flew to Russia to participate in a testimonial game and to do some sponsorship for a betting company, which, of course, has been frowned upon.

“Now, a big crisis has started in the last few hours.

“Even politicians got involved in Italy, saying that whoever represents Russia or helps Russia should never, never be appointed into public office. So you can imagine the things have unravelled.

“And Paolo Maldini, who's been in the job less than three weeks, might resign if Pirlo, his friend, is not appointed. I mean, there's never a boring moment in Italian football. Let's face it.”

Fisichella ended up being correct in his statement too, as Maldini has now gone on to step down from his position.

Sports.title: Chelsea lead race in shock move to sign Jordan Henderson on free transfer
Sports.content:
Chelsea lead race in shock move to sign Jordan Henderson on free transfer

Chelsea are working on a deal to sign England international Jordan Henderson, talkSPORT understands.

Brentford have given permission for the 36-year-old to leave on a free transfer this summer.

6 Chelsea are working on a deal to sign Henderson from Brentford on a free transfer Credit: Getty

Henderson is keen on a move to Stamford Bridge ahead of the new Premier League season.

Xabi Alonso's side currently lead the race to sign the veteran midfielder.

Having signed for the Bees on a two-year deal last summer, Henderson has less than 12 months remaining on his current deal.

The Liverpool legend, who boasts a Premier League winners' medal to his name made 32 league appearances last season, scoring once and adding three assists.

Blues target

He was also part of England's squad at this summer's World Cup in North America.

However, Henderson made just one appearance for the Three Lions, with his tournament ending early after surgery on a broken radius.

The injury, which he suffered celebrating England's last 16 win over Mexico, ruled Henderson out of the final three fixtures.

He was still able to collect a bronze medal following the third-place play-off win over France, though.

Henderson's move to Brentford in July 2025 followed spells with Ajax and Al Ettifaq since his Liverpool exit three years ago.

During his time at Anfield, he won eight major trophies including the Champions League, Premier League and Club World Cup.

6 Brentford are willing to allow Henderson to leave for free this summer Credit: Getty

6

Across spells with Liverpool, Sunderland and Brentford, Henderson has made a total of 463 Premier League appearances.

Meanwhile, he has scored 34 goals and provided 56 assists in those outings.

Chelsea transfer plans

Alonso's interest in Henderson comes as Chelsea weigh up a move for Brighton striker Danny Welbeck.

Talks are at an early stage between the two clubs regarding the veteran forward, talkSPORT understands.

Welbeck's Seagulls contract is currently set to expire at the end of June 2027.

Brighton would not stand in his way of an exit if a fee can be agreed.

6 Chelsea are also considering a surprise move for Brighton striker Welbeck Credit: Getty

Since joining the club in October 2020, Welbeck has scored 51 goals in 201 appearances across all competitions.

Last term saw the 35-year-old produce a career-high Premier League goal tally for the second year in a row after finding the net 13 times.

talkSPORT verdict

Ade Oladipo and Rory Jennings both reacted to the news of Chelsea's interest in Henderson on Drive.

Jennings had earlier claimed that Chelsea need an experienced title winner like Welbeck in the dressing room.

When Oladipo put those comments back to him, he replied: "I don't think we need a dressing room full of it."

The talkSPORT co-host continued: "I don't think you need to sign the England team of 2018. I don't think that's what we need to do.

6 Jennings doubts whether Henderson is the 'right answer' for Chelsea Credit: Getty

"I think what we need to do is bring in some standards for sure. I don't think Jordan Henderson is the right answer.

"I quite like Henderson. I don't necessarily rate him, but I quite like him.

"I think what he did for Liverpool was an integral part of their success. He was an integral part of everything that Jurgen Klopp built."

Jennings then added: "We've had a transfer strategy over the past four years where we've bought nothing but young, unproven footballers. Something needs to change. You need to equalise it.

"So I do understand what Xabi Alonso's problem is. I do understand why he's thinking about a way of resolving this. I would argue that Jordan Henderson isn't quite the answer.

"You know when it was Granit Xhaka? That made more sense to me. Granit Xhaka is still a good player, still a player that can do a job.

6 Chelsea have already completed the £117million signing of Morgan Rogers this summer Credit: Getty

"I'm not convinced that Jordan Henderson is the answer. I'm not convinced that he's ready to play at this level. The fact that we're linked with him is minorly troubling."

Chelsea were linked with a move for Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka earlier this summer, but have been issued with a firm hands-off warning.

Meanwhile, Alonso has already added to his squad with the British-record £117million addition of Morgan Rogers.

The England forward has joined the club from Aston Villa on a seven-year deal.

Sports.title: EFL set to demand change to landmark £1.5bn deal after Premier League clubs vote
Sports.content:
The Football League could be set to push back on a proposed ten-year deal with the Premier League worth £1.5billion.

That is according to football finance expert Kieran Maguire ahead of this week's vote.



3 Premier League clubs will vote this week on a proposed 10-year EFL deal worth £1.5billion Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Top-flight clubs will vote on the proposed 'New Deal' on Thursday, according to Sky News.

At least 14 of the 20 Premier League clubs must vote in favour of the plans before the proposals can be put to the EFL.

If approved, an initial annual payment of £100million would be made to EFL clubs before rising to more than £130million in year two.



That figure would then increase to £160million for the third year and remain at that amount for the remaining seven years of the agreement.

A lifeboat fund worth £20million will also be introduced to assist any EFL club which falls into administration.



However, clubs must spend 20 per cent of the money they receive through the 'New Deal' on infrastructure, as part of the proposal.

There are hopes that a binding agreement can be reached within weeks if the proposal is approved on Thursday.



How will the payments be funded?

There are currently two sources being proposed to help fund the £1.5billion deal.

The first would see the Premier League's levy on domestic transfers raised from four per cent to six per cent.

Meanwhile, there is also a proposal to gradually reduce the three-year parachute payments received by relegated clubs.

3 The EFL is currently opposed to the proposed funding agreement, says football finance expert Maguire Credit: Getty Images - Getty



Explaining how the deal would be funded, Maguire told talkSPORT on Monday: "It looks as if it’s going to be funded through a couple of sources.

"First of all, the levy, which arises on domestic transfers. That’s going to go up from four per cent to six per cent.

"So if you’re signing a £100million player, that’s an extra £2million which goes into the pot.

"Secondly, it looks as if parachute payments are going to be scaled down. I think that will please the EFL because ideally they’d like them abolished, but I think they acknowledge that they do serve a useful purpose."



EFL stance

Maguire continued: "So you put those sums together, plus the fact that the Premier League is very successful, I think it’s going to go through the £7billion barrier for the first time in season 2025/26.

"So all of that is more money coming into the game. The regulator doesn’t want to get involved, but this is an opportunity for the Premier League to show that it can negotiate with the EFL.

3 Reduced parachute payments and an increase to the Premier League's transfer levy are set to fund the plans Credit: Getty Images - Getty

"But first of all, it has to go for a vote of Premier League clubs and then we’ve got to see what the response of the EFL is."



Even if the Premier League clubs vote in favour of the proposed deal, the EFL could still push back on the terms put to them.

Maguire admits this could likely be the case based on the current composition of the proposal.

He added: "Certainly the noises coming out of the EFL aren’t that positive, but it certainly does look a step forward.

"Even though it might need further negotiating and sort of tapering off at some point."

Sports.title: The year in New York City that turned Andoni Iraola into a manager: Patrick Vieira's 'discipline and structure', an NFL playbook and the tactic that opened Liverpool boss' eyes to the modern game
Sports.content:
New York, concrete jungle where dreams are made of. And so it was for Andoni Iraola.

Though the Basque spent 14 years playing at Athletic Club in Bilbao, appearing 510 times for their first team and capped seven times by Spain, Iraola credits his year at New York City FC (NYCFC) as a crucial part of his journey.

It began in the summer of 2015, when Iraola lived in a swanky Manhattan apartment in the Upper West side, very close to the edge of Central Park, with his wife Itziar and their first daughter.

Iraola acknowledged this week that joining NYCFC, who are owned by Manchester City's City Football Group, was a key part of his career and formed his first step into coaching.

Playing under boss Patrick Vieira, his list of team-mates was a star-studded cast: Frank Lampard, Andrea Pirlo, David Villa.

Playing alongside that trio was instrumental in Iraola gaining a richer understanding of the game. As a right back for most of his career, he learned to invert to become a deep-lying midfielder when his team had the ball, which he believes opened his eyes more to the tactical side of the game.

New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola credits his year at New York City with helping his move into coaching

Iraola joined the City Football Group club at the same time as Frank Lampard

Iraola was part of a star-studded New York City team that included Andrea Pirlo and David Villa

At full back, he just had to keep tabs on the opposition left winger – now, he had to control everything. Seeing the game in this new light was important to Iraola’s tactical style, which he further forged managing in Cyprus and then Spain with Mirandes and Rayo Vallecano.

‘I was lucky enough to have Vieira as a coach and he made me see the game differently,’ Iraola told Daily Mail Sport in an exclusive interview in 2024. ‘We used to play almost like Manchester City. I started to understand the positional game better, the possession-based football. They are tools I’ve used after.

‘Patrick had discipline and structure. It definitely helped me a lot. In midfield you’ve got to be in touch with everyone. It demands a good understanding of the game and it’s not a coincidence that the very big coaches come from the midfield positions. There aren’t many full backs!’

Though Iraola learned many things on the pitch during his 40 appearances in Major League Soccer, it was on his days off that he would really thrive. Baseball, basketball, NFL, ice hockey, you name it, Iraola was there, and even now, he still plays an NFL version of fantasy football.

He believes that the tactical side of NFL was eye-opening in terms of the blocks, the spaces left open, exploiting areas of the pitch and the whole methodology of it which is similar to set-pieces. Iraola was fascinated by the playbook that teams have, sometimes reaching 200 set-plays, though he limits his set-pieces to four or five routines.

Aside from going to sporting events, the Liverpool boss would make a point of visiting a different neighbourhood each day that he had a free afternoon.

He would dine out with his wife in various New York districts – Williamsburg, in Brooklyn, was his favourite spot – and have a long lunch. The pair would make an effort to strike up conversations with strangers, which helped Iraola’s English.

When he retired as a player in November 2016 to begin his coaching journey, NYCFC’s official site published a glowing reference.

Iraola believes he started to see the game differently with a focus on possession-based football

Iraola had moved to MLS after a lengthy spell playing for Athletic Club in La Liga

Iraola played at right back for Athletic Club, but believes his understanding of the game was enhanced after switching to a deep-lying midfield role at New York City

‘His playing legacy will be of someone who was the epitome of consistent excellence and selfless teamwork,’ it read. ‘Off the pitch, he'll be remembered as a person who showed humility and professionalism every single day he was at the club.’

Manager Vieira said Iraola was the ‘perfect image of a team player’ and ‘everyone loves him’, while captain and former Spain World Cup winner Villa – who he is still friends with – said: ‘He is a wonderful person and player and I wish him all the best in the future. He knows he’ll have a friend for the rest of his life in me.’

Iraola has been back to New York City several times since leaving, including in the last two pre-seasons with Bournemouth. On Tuesday, he will be back for the second leg of Liverpool’s summer tour, taking on Wrexham here in the Big Apple.

For the new boss, it will be a chance to reflect on just how far he has come since those long lunches on the streets of Williamsburg and nights watching the Brooklyn Nets and New York Giants. It was in this city that the Liverpool manager forged his very own playbook for success.

Sports.title: Inside Arsenal's Hale End academy woes: Why two wonderkids have left, how Gunners missed out on Jeremy Monga, the target who's heading for Spurs instead and why first-team success is creating 'a perfect storm'
Sports.content:
Arsenal's rather unexciting first-team recruitment activity has dominated the summer chat in the pubs of north London. Their Hale End academy, however, has quietly endured its own transfer misery.

Despite being Premier League champions and boasting one of England's most celebrated youth set-ups, Arsenal have lost a string of key recruitment battles - from being beaten to top targets to seeing their own highly-rated prospects reject new deals.

First, Manchester City hijacked a move for promising Leicester City winger Jeremy Monga, whom Arsenal had been close to signing. Second, Tottenham are poised to beat the Gunners to West Ham’s Under-15 midfield star Isaac Allen.

And then internally, talented youngsters such as Kyran Thompson and Mishel Nduka have chosen to continue their careers elsewhere.

Behind the setbacks lies a changing academy market in which rival clubs are prepared to offer eye-watering salaries to 16-year-olds, while Arsenal remain reluctant to match those figures. Combined with an increasingly difficult pathway into Mikel Arteta's title-winning first team, it has created a perfect storm that is testing the club's renowned youth system.

Missing out on Monga first drew attention to this academy malaise. The 17-year-old Leicester star was on track to join the Gunners after the club registered their firm interest for weeks and put in the groundwork. Yet, City stole in amid Arsenal’s reluctance to meet Leicester’s £10million valuation. City paid £12.5m for the youngster.

Arsenal's academy players are put through their paces - but it has been a frustrating summer at Hale End

Arsenal missed out to Manchester City for the services of Jeremy Monga, with City agreeing to pay Leicester a higher fee

That hasn't been the only attempted transfer not to come to fruition.

As Daily Mail Sport reported last week, Tottenham are close to beating Arsenal to signing West Ham’s 15-year-old Allen. Again, the Gunners were keen on the player - but Spurs are now confident they will land him.

There are, meanwhile, a number of prospects Arsenal wanted to keep and have sign scholarship terms - with a view to a professional contract aged 17 - who have turned down deals. They include Thompson, the highly-rated 16-year-old winger who joined in 2024 after the club paid West Ham £1.1m.

Last season, Thompson was fast-tracked into the Under 18s, while also featuring for the Under 19s in UEFA’s Youth League - an academy version of the Champions League - and making his Under-21 debut in Premier League 2.

The Gunners saw a pathway for the teenager and were keen to tie him down to a new extended contract. Yet, as Daily Mail Sport reported, he turned it down and pursued a move to Spurs - before pivoting to join Newcastle.

Nduka falls into the same category. He joined the Arsenal academy in September 2025 after eight years at Charlton. The skilful midfielder, who turned 16 in April, made the Under 21s squad twice last season and also featured in a UEFA Youth League Under-19 match against Club Bruges in December.

He regularly appeared for the Under 18s, playing 10 games in a group above his own age, and shone. But he has now joined City.

Some young players cannot see a way into Arsenal's first team now that they are successful on the pitch

Myles Lewis-Skelly (left) and Bukayo Saka have helped build Hale End's reputation as a production line of elite talent

There are two factors influencing Arsenal’s predicament. The first is money. The likes of City are willing to pay way beyond the Gunners in wages for academy players. And that outlay does not count towards the Premier League's financial rules so clubs can, to a degree, throw what they want at these youngsters.

Daily Mail Sport understands Nduka’s City deal includes a salary of £20,000 a week, which puts the 16-year-old on around £1m a year. Monga, meanwhile, is understood to be on a much more lucrative wage.

Arsenal’s stance is that they are unwilling to pay salaries they believe are disproportionate for players yet to play senior top-flight football. Their focus is on development, building a genuine career pathway and potential re-sale value. But in reality, the academy landscape has changed.

The other element is a pathway to the first team. Some young players can’t see a way to the senior squad because of how well Arsenal have done on the pitch.

As reigning champions with a squad so strong the likes of Christian Norgaard played only a handful of games last season, earning a place in the set-up is extremely hard. This makes other clubs, like Tottenham for example, an attractive proposition.

Some players believe the pathway to first-team football is clearer at a club that narrowly avoided relegation in the last two seasons.

There have been some wins, though, in this window under new academy director Pascal De Maesschalck who was appointed earlier in the month. His arrival has helped steady the ship after uncertainty following Per Mertesacker’s departure, the club actively operating in the market.

Arsenal are close to completing the signing of Cardiff City teenager Axel Donczew.

The 16-year-old attacking midfielder made headlines last October when he became Cardiff’s youngest-ever senior player, aged just 15 years and 234 days old when he came on as a substitute in the Welsh club’s EFL Trophy game against Newport County.

Elijah Upson, the 18-year-old son of Matthew, last week signed for Arsenal from Spurs and has joined up with the Under 21s.

The Gunners are also pushing hard to acquire Crystal Palace striker Mylo Bernard, 16.

But the whole academy market is in a state of flux, turbo-charged by eye-watering sums and a desire by top clubs to seize the country’s best talents before they turn professional at 17.

Kyran Thompson, the highly-rated 16-year-old winger who joined the Gunners in 2024 from West Ham, turned down a new Arsenal contract to join Newcastle

Mishel Nduka joined the Arsenal academy in September 2025 after eight years at Charlton but has now moved to Manchester City, where his salary is £20,000 a week

For Arsenal, the challenge is complicated. Hale End has built a reputation for producing elite talent, with Bukayo Saka, Ethan Nwaneri and Myles Lewis-Skelly among the graduates to break into the first team in recent years.

The Gunners can point to their record of promoting youth, but the battle for the best young players is no longer simply about reputation or coaching. It is about money and opportunity.

For years, Hale End was viewed as one of Arsenal's greatest competitive advantages.

Now, as the club sits at the summit of English football, protecting that advantage is proving to be its next great challenge.

Sports.title: 'I don't even know what tomorrow looks like': Adam Ramsay-Peaty sends cryptic Olympics message after falling short of Commonwealth Games gold AGAIN as swimmer admits he has felt 'off' in Glasgow
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty dunked his head under the water, looked up at the scoreboard and smiled. His time, 26.94 seconds, was only enough for bronze but he did not beat himself up about it.

Throughout his career, Ramsay-Peaty has swum with the spirit of the giant lion tattooed on his bulging bicep. These Glaswegian waters will duly confess that age can tame the most vicious of animals.

‘My superpower looks very different now,’ said the 31-year-old, who was slow off the blocks and needed every dose of muscle memory to pull his way back into third.

‘Juggling babies with milk and having a toddler around is a different superpower. As a professional athlete, yeah, I’m still committed. I’ve been that person that wins all the time and it costs you pretty much everything. I wouldn’t say it’s worth it now.’

The killer instinct has been replaced by parenthood.

Peaty remains Britain’s best breaststroker but he does not fill international opponents with fear like he used to. The sands of time catch up with everyone.

Most swimmers peak in their early 20s. Even the great Michael Phelps, with his 6ft7in wingspan and size 14 feet, did not win another Olympic medal after the age of 31.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty reacts after winning bronze in the men's 50m breaststroke at the Commonwealth Games

His wife Holly was seen watching on as Ramsay-Peaty secured his second medal of the Games

Ramsay-Peaty, pictured with wife Holly, had earlier labelled sport 'cruel' in an emotional statement

Ariane Titmus won four Olympic golds and here, aged 25, she is standing poolside with a microphone, carrying out post-race interviews for Australia’s national broadcaster.

Ramsay-Peaty’s finish time was almost a whole second off his world record. He accepted his bronze medal with grace, waving to his adoring Glaswegian audience, and he was more interested in taking home the cuddly unicorn for his son.

‘For me, that period of time when I was undefeated for eight years, or whatever it was, it was athlete first and then human,’ he said. ‘Now it’s human first and then athlete. That’s a good gamble. We don’t really know what the outcome’s going to be. We obviously need to switch up what we’re doing in training to a certain extent. I’ve been in my new training base 12 weeks so let’s keep it in perspective.’

Two lanes to his right, Scoland’s Archie Goodburn was swimming with terminal cancer. Doctors found three inoperable brain tumours two years ago and his presence offered a dose of perspective for the man whose life has turned into a swimming pool soap opera.

There is nothing glamourous about competing in Glasgow. Events finish late and start early in what feels like a tarted-up leisure centre. Sleep is a luxury. Ramsay-Peaty has been catching the double decker bus to Tollcross with his fellow swimmers. Single fares on the local First Bus service normally cost £2.45. No VIP shuttles here. With no road closures, the traffic tends to bottleneck at the turning off Wellcross Road, allowing plenty of thinking time

After missing out on gold over 100m on Saturday night, Ramsey-Peaty questioned the sacrifices required for this life. “What’s the point of all the 5.30ams? What’s the point of all the metres every day? What’s the point of feeling exhausted all the time? What’s the point of saying, “No” to all the family events because of training?” Time will tell how strong his appetite remains for mouthfuls of chlorine.

Ramsay-Peaty spoke of the importance of fatherhood as he and Holly expect their first child

The legendary British swimmer took to social media with a lengthy statement on Monday

The 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, at least, offer a more glamorous proposition. The swimming meets will be staged at the SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, which most recently hosted the World Cup quarter-final between Spain and Belgium. The 100,000-square-foot NFL field will be transformed into the largest swimming venue in Olympic history. Perhaps the idea of a family trip to the West Coast to watch dad’s final race will make it all worthwhile.

‘There’s been a lot of learning this week,’ he said. ‘

‘I said it in Birmingham but this is absolutely my last Commonwealths. I just went out there and enjoyed it – really enjoyed it – but we just weren’t fast enough, weren’t good enough. We have to look at why, because the data this season has been tracking on an upward trend.

‘I can’t really put my finger on it, where I just lost that power to the stroke. Something’s not kicking but I’ve got to learn from it. To get two bronzes, with a relay to go, I’d say that’s success. I’m not going to be too hard on myself, not anymore.’

Earlier, on TNT Sports, he admitted: 'I don't even know what tomorrow looks like really, there's a lot of learning. I've felt 'off' this week and I don't know why. We are trying new things.'

This is not the fastest pool on the swimming circuit. Most modern elite Olympic swimming pools are three metres deep but the waves in this shallower, two-metre basin can add a few tenths of a second to finish times.

Ramsay-Peaty’s comments after his 100m race on Saturday night raised eyebrows among some of his peers. He claimed he deserved more. He felt his input – physical and mental – warranted more than a third-place finish. Several athletes accused him of arrogance and entitlement. They wake up just as early and train just as hard, but last night it felt like he had been away for a reality check.

When the adrenaline is still pumping through his body after races, Ramsay-Peaty sometimes says things he regrets. He can be unfiltered. His post on Instagram before the race was perhaps more measured. ‘I know this story won’t be filled with glory, victory and gold,’ he wrote. ‘However I’ll keep fighting, learning, adapting and striving for excellence until I can no longer give anymore. Sport isn’t a fairytale if your happiness and self-worth are only validated by medals. But it can be, if you find value in the hardship, the struggle and the tough times which might ultimately lead you to what you seek.'

He spent Sunday morning scribbling notes in his hotel room in Glasgow. ‘Am I good enough? Am I not good enough?’ asked the monkey in the back of his mind. He is now chasing the pack – as well as his younger self – yet he remains one of sport’s greatest showman. When the Chinese, American, Dutch join him in the pool, the chase will not get any easier.

Sports.title: Inside Vinicius Junior's commercial empire: How Brazilian icon and Arsenal target's SIXTEEN sponsors make him Real Madrid's most lucrative asset - and why the club take HALF of his brand earnings
Sports.content:
Real Madrid are reaping huge financial rewards from Vinicius Junior's vast sponsorship portfolio, with the Brazilian having established himself as one of world football's most marketable goldmines in recent seasons.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday that Arsenal are ambitiously exploring a bombshell swoop for Vinicius Junior this summer, should he fail to agree a new contract at the Bernabeu.

The Brazilian international, who will currently be out of contract at the Bernabeu at the end of the 2027-28 season, did not show for pre-season training on Monday while his representatives hold crunch talks with Real Madrid in an attempt to strike an agreement over a new deal.

Madrid, while unwilling to put the 26-year-old on the same salary as team-mate Kylian Mbappe, will be eager to keep him on their books because of his global superstar status, underlined by an impressive list of 16 commercial partnerships.

Among players who competed at this summer's World Cup, Vinicius Junior was second only to Neymar for the most sponsorship deals at the tournament, who boasts 20.

Content Vinicius posted on social media to promote these brands amassed well over 100 million views since his World Cup call-up, after he established himself as a poster boy for both Brazil and Real Madrid.

Since his arrival at the Bernabeu in 2018, Vinicius Junior has signed lucrative contract agreements with brands including Gatorade, Pepsi, Prada, PlayStation, UNESCO, Visa and Nike.

Real Madrid are reaping huge financial rewards from Vinicius Junior's sponsorship portfolio

The forward has a remarkable 16 sponsorship deals with global brands including Pepsi (above)

The Real Madrid and Brazil star also boasts a sponsorship with global sports brand Nike

He is also sponsored by Boss, Clear, Omo, Rexona, Betnacional, Dubai Tourism, Havaianas, Vivo and Marriot Bonvoy – taking his commercial empire to 16 companies.

According to Spanish outlet AS, when Vinicius Junior signed his 2022 contract renewal which is set to expire in the summer of 2027, he agreed to give Real Madrid approximately 50 per cent of his image rights.

Every penny Vinicius Junior earns commercially is thus split in half and shared with the LaLiga giants, making him one of the largest goldmines in world football.

As the Spanish newspaper jokes, Vinicius Junior is effectively paying his own salary at the Bernabeu, at least until a new agreement is struck between the club and player.

The Brazilian's commercial empire could therefore present a potential stumbling block in contract talks on Monday, and Arsenal's bombshell interest in the forward will undoubtedly provide Vinicius Junior with suitable leverage during the negotiations.

Frederico Pena, chief executive officer of Vinicius Junior's agency Roc Nation Sports Brazil, admitted his client has now achieved a status comparable to that of a business.

'Despite his young age, Vini is already a key player at the biggest club in the world and on the most important national team,' Pena said.

'He has been a champion and star player in two Champions Leagues, and is a role model of resilience and sporting success for most Brazilians. Furthermore, he doesn't shy away from important social issues, whether through his stance or his contributions to his community. All of this means that the number of brands interested in his image continues to grow.

Gatorade (left) and Prada (right) are also part of the Brazilian's lucrative sponsorship empire

Vinicius Jnr endorsing video game juggernauts PlayStation on his his Instagram account

'There is a structure with a CEO, a CFO, and administrative, legal, commercial, marketing, and communications departments that control everything.

'There are dozens of initiatives involving his numerous sponsors, in addition to social activities centered around his institute, which is now a global leader in innovative teaching methods for children and young people, as well as in teacher training focused on anti-racist pedagogical practices.'

His explosive talents on the football pitch may drive Real Madrid closer to trophies and titles but Vinicius Junior's true value lies in the commercial empire he has built off it.

Sports.title: Sean McCann, younger brother of Madeleine, takes to the pool again at the Commonwealth Games as proud parents Gerry and Kate watch on - but he finishes far off the medals in the 800m freestyle
Sports.content:
Sean McCann, younger brother of Madeleine, takes to the pool again at the Commonwealth Games as proud parents Gerry and Kate watch on - but he finishes far off the medals in the 800m freestyle

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The family of Madeleine McCann cheered on her younger brother Sean as he competed in the 800m men's freestyle at the Commonwealth Games.

Fresh off his stunning 400m effort, which saw the 21-year-old earn a surprise place in the final, McCann attempted to back up that performance in the longer discipline in Glasgow.

His parents Kate and Gerry and twin sister Amelie watched proudly as they cheered him on.

In what was essentially a time trial, McCann was seeded in the 'fastest' heat alongside superstars Sam Short and Daniel Wiffen, but finished in last place in the eight-strong field.

His time of 8:11.34 was nearly 32 seconds slower than Australian star Short, who took home the gold medal. Overall, McCann finished ninth out of 14 athletes.

Gerry was spotted wearing the football shirt of his beloved Everton Football Club, while Kate wore a swimming t-shirt.

Sean McCann was unable to accomplish a miracle feat in the pool at the Commonwealth Games

His parents Gerry (left) and Kate (right) watched on with twin sister Amelia (centre) as he finished ninth in the men's 800m freestyle

He is the younger brother of missing Madeleine McCann and was in the room when she was abducted from her family's holiday villa in Portugal in 2007

Almost two decades on from the infamous Portugal family holiday which saw Madeleine abducted, the McCann family's unimaginable tragedy still haunts him and Amelie, wherever they go.

Sean's mother Kate has previously told how he 'hated' the water when he was first taken swimming – and yet he soon found his drive, attending up to nine two-hour training sessions every week, many requiring 4am starts.

Inspired by his sporting family – Kate and Gerry even went on a run on their first date – Sean's dedication has paid off as he sets his sights on success in his first major international meet.

Sean came fourth in his heat and was cheered on today by both parents, as well as Amelie, who herself competes regularly in triathlons.

The elite distance swimmer is eligible to represent Scotland through his father, who was born in Glasgow.

This week a former member of Sean's coaching team told the Daily Mail that the combination of a young man who was 'really driven and never one to take the easiest route', and parents who willed him on, had made him a powerhouse and his story an inspiration.

In his teenage years Sean's parents would ferry him to training sessions at Braunstone Leisure Centre, a 20-minute drive from the family home in Rothley, Leicestershire, where he would clock up an impressive amount of swim sessions a week, plus two or three punishing gym workouts.

McCann was unable to trouble the podium positions, with gold medal winner Sam Short finishing nearly 32 seconds ahead

Kate and Gerry 'encouraged their children, but didn't push them' said the insider, who coached Sean as a youngster.

He remembered the young man being focused on the Commonwealth Youth Games in Trinidad in 2023 and then deciding he wanted to race for Scotland and for GB in open-water events – so for swimming competitively he changed his nationality to Scottish.

'For the Commonwealth Games, I was lucky enough to be at the trials in London when he was racing. It was great to watch him and talk to him between prep, to be a part of it and see his journey unfold,' he said.

What a journey, too, for Sean, who is studying chemical engineering at Loughborough University – chosen for its unrivalled sports facilities.

Distance swimming is an unforgiving sport. Yet those who know Sean's career describe a steady, determined progression, even during the Covid-19 lockdown when he would train out of the pool at home with Amelie, who is also a keen swimmer.

In the 2023 Commonwealth Youth Games, he reached the finals of the 400m and 1,500m freestyle, and has since qualified for the European Open Water Championships representing Great Britain.

Sean himself said this week that he was 'very excited' about the challenges ahead. 'It's the pinnacle really - of representing Scotland in the Commonwealth Games, and especially at a home games.

'I've got lots of family up in Glasgow so that makes it even more special. I was there in 2014 watching as a kid, so to make it now, 12 years later, is really a full circle moment.

'It's my first senior games, so I'm just looking forward to be representing Scotland and doing my absolute best. I always tend to go out quite slow and build my way into a race. That's just how I like to pace it.'

It's quite the change from what Sean has been known for by many until now, solely for his close proximity to Madeleine's disappearance.

The young Scot, 21, is aiming to represent Team GB at the Olympic Games in Los Angeles

He was, after all, in the same room when she was abducted from the family's holiday apartment in Praia da Luz in 2007 when he was just two.

Although he might not remember the international fallout, both siblings have grown up in the shadow of the mystery surrounding their older sister, who would now be 23.

The McCann parents have repeatedly spoken of their determination to ensure that Sean and Amelie could grow up with the most normal childhood possible.

'Our worry is for our children,' Kate said in 2017. 'I think we've tried to educate them a little bit as well because obviously it's not just us that has fallen victim to the downside of social media.

'At some point you've got to realise that time is not frozen and I think both of us realise that we owed it to the twins to make sure that their life is as fulfilling as they deserve, and we have certainly tried our best to achieve that.'

Gerry also spoke about developing their independence. 'I am certainly more protective than I was, but you can't mollycoddle them,' he said.

'They have to be independent. There is increased anxiety but we can't let that impact on them having a normal upbringing. Sean and Amelie are doing really really well; obviously they are not immune to the media, they hear things, they go to school, they hear the radio.'

For Sean, and by extension his whole family, this is his opportunity to step into the light of something new. The young swimmer is only just getting started – he has the 800m and 1,500m freestyle to follow.

Sports.title: Besiktas chief claims Mohamed Salah talks have broken down after meeting THREE times with Liverpool legend's camp
Sports.content:
Besiktas chief claims Mohamed Salah talks have broken down after meeting THREE times with Liverpool legend's camp

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Besiktas director Onder Ozen has claimed the Turkish club have walked away from talks with Liverpool legend Mohamed Salah despite meeting his camp three times.

Salah is a free agent this summer after agreeing with Liverpool to rip up the final year of his contract, ending a trophy-laden spell on Merseyside.

The Egyptian star had been approached by Besiktas over a move with the club's president Serdal Adali telling Turkish media they were awaiting a final decision.

Besiktas have now reportedly ended talks with Salah's camp, claiming a deadlock in negotiations.

Ozen suggested Salah's representatives are in talks with another club but stressed their final offer remained on the table if they wished to resume talks.

'We contacted Salah, this also involved a financing model,' Ozen told Turkish media.

Besiktas have claimed they have walked away from negotiations with Mohamed Salah

'Salah is a global star, a respected athlete. We met with Salah three times before the financial part of the negotiations was discussed.

'Up to this point, everything was smooth. When the financial side began, the initial smoothness slowed down from July 21st onwards.

'Requests began to arrive that would both disrupt the flow of information and create a deadlock in the financial process. I can assume that a respected athlete like Salah was unaware of this.

'The club has a policy, and it cannot deviate from that policy, our President has very clearly identified his position and has stayed there.

'I don't have a chance to say yes or no, Besiktas's offer, made under its own terms, is clear. If a response comes to this offer, it can be evaluated.

'But Besiktas will not make another offer. They said they are also in talks with another club, maybe they will get a result from there.

'The last offer we made to Salah is the final point that does not harm Besiktas's club identity.'

Salah, now 34, has offers from elsewhere including in Major League Soccer, where Sporting Kansas City have made a lucrative two-year contract proposal.

Sports.title: Leeds close in on James Trafford, Inter Milan near two-year deal for John Stones and Chelsea move for 36-year-old Jordan Henderson: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Leeds close in on James Trafford, Inter Milan near two-year deal for John Stones and Chelsea move for 36-year-old Jordan Henderson: WINDOW WATCH

For all of yesterday's developments - including Liverpool's push for a compromise on PSG's Bradley Barcola - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Black Cats target Methalie

Sunderland are continuing talks with Toulouse over full-back Dayann Methalie.

The 20-year-old was a target for Newcastle United at the turn of the year but picked up an untimely knee injury.

Now fully fit, Toulouse want around £25million for the France Under 21 international left back.

Hogh completes Celtic medical ahead of club-record deal

Celtic are finalising the club record £11million signing of Bodo/Glimt striker Kasper Hogh.

The Denmark international completed a medical in London today and is due to finalise a four-year deal tomorrow, with Celtic having the option to extend by a further year.

Celtic are finalising the club record £11million signing of Bodo/Glimt striker Kasper Hogh

Leeds close in on Trafford

Leeds United are finalising an agreement on a £40million transfer, plus £5m in add-ons and a sell-on clause, for Manchester City goalkeeper James Trafford.

The deal is not complete, but positive talks are continuing and are expected to reach the final stages imminently.

The 23-year-old is keen on the move to Leeds and sees it as a chance to play regularly and establish himself as England's No 1.

Discussions have taken place over a release clause, with other top Premier League sides willing to monitor his development.

Newcastle had discussed an offer for Trafford but have switched their sights. They are assessing Sporting Braga's Lukas Hornicek among others.

Despite holding a meeting regarding Brighton's Carl Rushworth, Newcastle were understood to have had reservations about his top-flight experience.

Discussions have taken place over a release clause, with other top Premier League sides willing to monitor Trafford's development

Leeds' previous record-signing was Georginio Rutter from Hoffenheim for around £35.5m in January 2023.

Torino remain keen to sign Leeds’ Lucas Perri once terms are agreed on Trafford.

Manchester City are also working to add a new goalkeeper.

Stones close to Inter Milan deal

England defender John Stones is close to agreeing a two-year contract with Inter Milan.

The 32-year-old is a free agent after leaving Manchester City and has had interest from a number of clubs, including Chelsea, Arsenal and Juventus.

However, Inter are proposing a two-year deal and want to team him up with Tottenham's Cristian Romero, whose agent held talks over the weekend.

Inter had also considered Chelsea's Trevoh Chalobah and sounded out Spurs' Djed Spence.

Stones proved his fitness at the World Cup and Inter believe his experience and reading of the game will complement their style as they challenge for the Serie A title and the Champions League.

He is keen on trying a new culture and is leaning towards an agreement as talks reach an advanced stage.

Stones proved his fitness at the World Cup and Inter believe his experience and reading of the game will complement their style

Chelsea move for Henderson

Chelsea are working on a deal to sign Jordan Henderson on a free transfer from Brentford.

After missing out on Sunderland’s Granit Xhaka, the Stamford Bridge club have moved for 36-year-old Henderson to fulfil a role on the pitch and crucially in the dressing room.

As Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed, Chelsea are already closing on a move for Danny Welbeck as manager Xabi Alonso looks to add older heads to a young squad.

Alonso has determined that the squad dynamic needs to change to help Chelsea achieve their goals and maintain a successful challenge to rivals.

There are a number of clubs interested in Henderson, who is still recovering from a fractured arm suffered during the World Cup, including two other Premier League sides, but Chelsea are favourites to sign him.

After missing out on Sunderland’s Granit Xhaka, Chelsea have moved for 36-year-old Henderson to fulfil a role on the pitch and crucially in the dressing room

Barca keep Kroupi on their radar

Barcelona remain attentive to Eli Junior Kroupi's situation as their proposed deal for Julian Alvarez continues to prove tricky to conclude.

Bournemouth insist he is not for sale but the forward is on Barcelona’s radar as well as that of Arsenal and Manchester City.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Barca's interest in Kroupi in May.

Eli Junior Kroupi in Bournemouth's pre-season training today in Austria

Imray's set for £4.5m Wrexham deal

Wrexham are closing in on signing full back Danny Imray from Crystal Palace in a £4.5m deal.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport yesterday the 22-year-old, who had loan spells with Blackpool and West Bromwich Albion last season, was wanted back by Albion while Stoke City also posted interest.

Wrexham, though, have got their man as they look to bolster their bid for promotion from the Championship to the Premier League.

Wycombe made a £750k bid in January 2025, which Palace decided to rebuff. Now they are set to land a fee seven-times higher 18 months later.

Additional reporting: BOBBY MANZI

Crystal Palace's Danny Imray has been a target for more than one EFL club

Chelsea line up Welbeck

Chelsea are interested in signing Danny Welbeck, Daily Mail Sport can reveal.

The 35-year-old Brighton striker has emerged as a player of interest within Stamford Bridge, and is now a contender to join the Blues squad under Xabi Alonso.

Welbeck has scored 46 goals in 176 games in the Premier League for the Seagulls, having previously played for Manchester United and Arsenal, among others.

Read more on this story HERE

KIERAN GILL

Danny Welbeck was considered unfortunate to miss out on England's World Cup squad

Wolves' Tolu set for exit after training drama

Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare is joining Ajax on loan with view to a £17million permanent deal.

Ajax have to cover his salary in full on top of a £1m loan fee and have agreed further bonuses if they qualify for European competitions.

Last week, Arokodare forced the cancellation of a Wolves training session after he refused to leave the pitch.

Read more on this story HERE

Tolu Arokodate trains in Portugal earlier this month

Vasquez set to join Blues

Argentinian striker Luis Vazquez is joining Birmingham City from Anderlecht.

The 25-year-old was on loan at Getafe last season but is joining Birmingham permanently for a fee of around £3million.

Read all about it as Forest eye £21m deal

Nottingham Forest are continuing negotiations with Feyenoord over a £21million deal for Givairo Read.

The Netherlands U21 international right back has agreed a five-year contract with Forest but they have still to finalise terms with his club after improving their offer on Sunday.

Feyenoord ideally want to keep the right-back for another season but he is keen on the move to the Premier League and what would be a hefty increase in salary.

Ortega in talks over Greece move

Former Nottingham Forest and Manchester City goalkeeper Stefan Ortega is in advanced talks with Olympiacos.

The 33-year-old left Forest in June after the expiry of his short-term contract.

The Greek club are also owned by Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis and are selling Konstantinos Tzolakis to Hull City.

Stefan Ortega left Forest this summer after his short-term contract ended

Manchester United sign new keeper

Manchester United have confirmed the signing of goalkeeper Kit Margetson from Swansea.

The 20-year-old was on loan at Welsh Premier League side Connah’s Quay Nomads last season, where he kept 10 clean sheets in 34 appearances.

The Wales youth keeper, the son of former Manchester City keeper Martyn Margetson, made his debut for Wales U21s against Belarus in March.

Margetson will move to Old Trafford subject to registration, after the two clubs agreed a compensation deal.

Kit Margetson is the son of former Manchester City keeper Martyn and also plays in goal

Ipswich land giant keeper Kjell

Ipswich Town have agreed a fee of around £11million for 6ft 9in Dutch goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen.

Scherpen had his medical today ahead of becoming their sixth new signing of the summer.

The fee agreed with his club Union Saint-Gilloise is £8.5m plus a further £2.5m in add-ons.

Brighton also had a 40 percent sell-on clause from USG as part of the deal.

Kjell Scherpen spent four years as a Brighton player from 2021 but spent most of his time out on loan

Villa's Kosta eyed by Osasuna

Aston Villa defender Kosta Nedeljkovic is wanted on loan by Osasuna.

The 20-year-old Serbia international right-back has been on loan at RB Leipzig but has not had a great deal of game time owing to niggly back and knee injuries.

He returned to full fitness in March and played for Serbia against World Cup winners Spain and was back in Villa's team for the pre-season friendly win over Walsall last week.

Fiorentina also made enquiries for Nedeljkovic earlier this year but Villa are ready to send him out for what they hope will be a more beneficial season on loan and La Liga side Osasuna want him to join them.

Villa have been trying to add another right-back and held talks with Flamengo for former Spurs defender Emerson Royal.

They are still to receive another approach from Arsenal for Ezri Konsa but the offer of a new contract is on the table and they do not need to sell following the £117m departure of Morgan Rogers.

Leicester eye Spurs defender Hardy
