Tottenham defensive prospect Malachi Hardy has emerged as a potential loan target for Leicester City.

The League One side are exploring a move for the England U18 international who has impressed Roberto de Zerbi on pre-season so far with his composure and ability.

Following the 2-0 win over Auckland, De Zerbi said simply of the central defender, 'Malachi is another good player for the future of the club.'

The 18-year-old was given a contract extension earlier this year after impressing staff enough to step up to train with the first team and 'improving his aggression'.

Everton's Ndiaye a target for Al-Hilal

Al-Hilal are targeting Everton winger Iliman Ndiaye.

The Senegal international, 26, has three years left on his contract and Everton have been trying to tie him down to an improved deal which he has so far rejected.

The club’s stance has been he is not for sale amid interest from Premier League rivals but Al Hilal’s presence and financial power may bring greater concern.

Much will depend on what offer they put on the table, but they have yet to submit a bid.

Al Hilal, who have former Bournemouth technical director Simon Francis now on their staff, signed Crysencio Summerville from West Ham last week.

Sports.title: Italian football in CHAOS as Paolo Maldini and Leonardo QUIT after Andrea Pirlo was blocked from becoming new national team coach amid links to Russian betting firm
Sports.content:
Italian football in CHAOS as Paolo Maldini and Leonardo QUIT after Andrea Pirlo was blocked from becoming new national team coach amid links to Russian betting firm

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Italian football has been rocked by the news that Paolo Maldini and Leonardo have quit in the wake of Andrea Pirlo being ruled out of the running as next national team boss.

Pirlo is no longer in the frame to become Italy's next manager after 'political' concerns were raised over the football legend's sponsorship deal with a Russian betting company.

Pirlo, 47, was backed by former team-mate and new Italian Football Federation (FIGC) technical director Maldini to land the role after legendary ex-Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola reportedly declined the opportunity.

The former AC Milan and Juventus star was on the brink of agreeing a deal with the crisis-hit football nation before several Italian politicians raised concerns about Pirlo's role as an ambassador for Russian betting firm Fonbet.

It was felt Pirlo, who had been prepared to leave his current job as coach of Dubai United, should not have conflicting views on Italy's support for Ukraine in the war with Russia.

In the subsequent fallout, Maldini and his assistant Leonardo are reported to have stepped down, too, after just 16 days in their jobs.

Pirlo himself confirmed that he was no longer in the running in an Instagram post on Monday, urging that his Fonbet deal was linked to his job in the United Arab Emirates and is 'exclusively for commercial and sports' purposes.

His claim has been refuted by Dubai United owner Sergey Lomakin, who stated that Pirlo's involvement with the firm was not an involuntary aspect of his deal.

Andrea Pirlo is no longer in the running to become Italy's next manager after a dramatic twist

The Italy legend's appointment has been blocked after 'political' concerns were raised over his sponsorship deal with Russian betting company Fonbet in the United Arab Emirates

Pirlo said in a statement: 'In recent days, I have witnessed with great bitterness the debate that has developed around my name and the possibility of taking on the role of Head Coach of the Italian national team.

'Out of respect for the institutions, the Federation, and all those involved, I have chosen to remain silent until now.'

'However, I feel it is my duty to clarify certain aspects.

'Throughout my career, first as a player and now as a coach, I have always conducted my activities in full compliance with the laws of the countries in which I have worked and the contracts I have signed.

'The professional collaboration at the centre of the recent controversy arose as part of my career in the United Arab Emirates and is exclusively of a commercial and sporting nature.'

It is understood Maldini was furious by the decision made by FIGC president Giovanni Malago and quit his role as technical director after Pirlo's appointment was blocked.

Adverts, endorsements and sponsorship deals pertaining to betting are strictly prohibited in Italy.

Pirlo added: 'Attributing political meaning to this collaboration means attributing to me beliefs I have never expressed and that are not mine.

'I would like to thank Maldini and Leonardo for the esteem and trust they have shown me. I know their expertise, their seriousness, and the love they have always dedicated to Italian football.

Paolo Maldini was furious at the decision and has decided to walk away from his role as a result

'I regret that a sporting decision was quickly dragged into a public debate that ended up attributing to me meanings and intentions that are not mine.

'My love for Italy does not depend on a position. It is part of my history, my identity, and will continue to accompany me, always.'

Pirlo was at best a third-choice after Carlo Ancelotti and Guardiola turned down offers to coach a team that has failed to qualify for three consecutive World Cups.

Now former Italy coaches Roberto Mancini and Antonio Conte are back being discussed for the job.

Sports.title: Archie Goodburn breaks down after Commonwealth Games final two years after incurable brain cancer diagnosis
Sports.content:
Archie Goodburn breaks down after Commonwealth Games final two years after incurable brain cancer diagnosis

The Scottish breaststroke record holder broke down in tears after his final and he delivered a powerful message about brain cancer just two years on from his diagnosis

View 3 Images The swimmer broke down in tears after the final

An emotional Archie Goodburn broke down after the Comonwealth Games final as he declared his biggest dream comes outside of the pool, where brain cancer isn’t the biggest killer of those under 40.

‌



The Scottish swimmer fought back the tears after competing in the men's 50m breaststroke final on Monday.

‌



Although he came joint last in the race, and competed against English legend Adam Ramsay-Peaty, Edinburgh born Goodburn stole the show.

‌



View 3 Images A powerful message from a powerful athlete, living with the unimaginable. Archie Goodburn finished seventh in the Men’s 50m Breaststroke final at Glasgow 2026, two years after being told he has incurable brain cancer.

Even before entering the pool, Goodburn was met with a roaring ovation, being labelled "inspirational" by his team mates.

Two years ago, the Scottish 50m breaststroke record holder found out the devastating news of his diagnosis after a training session.

‌



He had been having some issues impacting his training including seizures and numbness on his left side.

He had been for some tests and missed a call whilst in the pool.

When he called back he was told he had brain cancer.

‌



The 22-year-old was told that he may not make it to his 40s.

View 3 Images GLASGOW, SCOTLAND - JULY 26: Archie Goodburn of team Scotland competes in the semi final of the Men's 50m Breaststroke during day three of the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games at Tollcross International Swimming Centre on July 26, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Following Monday's race, Goodburn broke down in to tears as he delivered an extremely powerful message.

‌



He said: "Outside the pool I dream of a future where brain cancer isn’t the biggest killer of those under 40.

"Where the UK government establish a brain cancer lead to make that change.

"I'd much prefer that change is made and that dream is completed than any of my personal goals in the pool because what families and young people are going through out there is really beyond the comprehension of many people out there and certainly harder than anything I’ve had to do as a world class sportsman."

‌



Goodburn has been having new treatments, which he fought to be able to receive, and they have slowed down the growth of his tumours.

The swimmer recently graduated from Edinburgh University with a first in chemical engineering.

After qualifying for the final he told BBC Sport Scotland that the past 24 hours has been "pretty indescribable".

Article continues below

Goodburn added: "Usually the words flow easily, but I'm finding myself quite speechless."

The Games became a focus for Goodburn during the tough times, but rather than just focus on himself he used the opportunity to talk passionately about guaranteeing brain cancer research is fully funded.

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty claims 'nothing makes sense' after Commonwealth Games double bronze
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty claims 'nothing makes sense' after Commonwealth Games double bronze

Adam Ramsay-Peaty has bemoaned the Commonwealth bronze he achieved on Monday and insists his training is worthy of a greater result

View 2 Images Adam Ramsay-Peaty has been outspoken about his results at the Commonwealth Games

Adam Ramsay-Peaty has claimed that his Commonwealth results "would be a lot better" if they actually reflected his training.

‌



The Brit had to settle for bronze in the 50m breaststroke, which comes days after he also finished third in the 100m event. It represents a drop for the athlete who dominated the sport previously and came into the event as the defending champion following his success four years ago.

‌



Ramsay-Peaty has had to try and rediscover the form he showed when he dominated the breaststroke events but was twice beaten by Australia's Sam Williamson.

‌



The 31-year-old was much more measured on Monday night having had to fight back the tears on Saturday when he came up short, but still felt his work didn't marry up with his performances.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty secures another Commonwealth bronze in 50m breaststroke READ MORE :

He said: "I am working way too hard. If those results were how much I am working then they would be a lot better. I need to look at that and adjust course because we are sailing in some rough seas right now and it is not sustainable. I have come back from worse and we will see where we end up."

He finished the race in 26.94 seconds - 0.44 behind Williamson - despite suggesting that the 50m event provided him with a better chance of success given it was a shorter distance and he was not north of 30.

‌



Ramsay-Peaty has been at a loss to explain some of his performances but remains determined to head to the Olympics in Los Angeles in four years time.

View 2 Images The 31-year-old finished third behind Michael Houlie and winner Sam Williamson

"I thought I could have done better there," he said after finishing third. "It is quite disappointing in terms of the time, and, as we know, times equal medals. I felt I could have been a little quicker, but I need to look at it and see where it is going on because nothing makes sense this week to be honest."

Article continues below

Since proving himself as one of the all-time greats Ramsay-Peaty has undergone huge life changes, marrying Holly Ramsay, whom is pregnant with his second child. His first, George, came from a previous relationship.

When he was dominating it owed to the coaching of Mel Marshall, who relocated to Australia in 2024. He has now moved back to London to work under Lisa Bates and will embark on a period of reflection.

"It is hard work, but we need to make sure that hard work is going in the right place," he said. "These things don't happen in three months; they happen in two years and we need to make sure we keep investing."

Sports.title: John Stones decides next club after England star holds talks with Chelsea
Sports.content:
John Stones decides next club after England star holds talks with Chelsea

John Stones is eyeing his next club after leaving Manchester City at the end of the season and, despite talks with Chelsea, has decided on his next move

View 2 Images John Stones has turned down the chance to sign for Chelsea

John Stones has decided to move abroad following his Manchester City exit despite holding talks with Chelsea over a possible switch.

‌



The England centre-half has just called time on his decade at the Etihad, which saw him win the Premier League on six occasions as well as the Champions League. The 32-year-old remains a strong performer and wasn't shy of suitors this summer.

‌



Chelsea were keen to add his quality and experience to their ranks with Xabi Alonso now in charge and multiple rounds of talks were held with the Blues. Ultimately Stones rejected the prospect of a move to Stamford Bridge to pursue his ambitions of playing elsewhere in Europe.

‌



Stones has played for Barnsley, Everton and City but is now closing in on a move to Inter Milan, according to reports. An agreement in principle has been secured with the Englishman, who has agreed on a deal until 2028.

Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing READ MORE :

Inter will go into the campaign as defending champions having won Serie A, their second Italian title in the last three years. They currently boast no English players in their ranks but a move to the San Siro would allow Stones to reignite his relationship with Manuel Akanji, whom he played with at City.

‌



Another Three Lions defender in Fikayo Tomori is playing at city rivals AC Milan, where he's been since 2021, although he is being linked with a move away.

Stones will bring the ball-playing ability that first attracted Pep Guardiola, who encouraged him to adopt more of a midfield role during his time in Manchester.

View 2 Images Inter Milan are poised to add the England defender

Article continues below

The veteran defender spoke in glowing terms about his time in Manchester, where he helped the club enjoyed their most successful period ever. He said: “It’s been a roller coaster. You can look at it like that and everything has ups and downs and good things, bad things. But to live out all my dreams and all my goals and all the things that I set out to achieve as a player and live as a player.

“Doing that has just been a dream and to be able to give that to everyone and do it in the style and fashion that we have and make everyone’s dream come true with obviously that Treble season, something that the club’s never achieved or won. It’s been so special.”

Sports.title: Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood
Sports.content:
Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood

The 23-year-old will ride at Group race level for the first time with rides on unbeaten two-year-olds in Tuesday's Vintage Stakes and Wednesday's Molecomb Stakes

View 3 Images Kaiya Fraser: has his first Group ride on Dr Rascal at Goodwood (Image: Maureen McLean/Shutterstock)

Kaiya Fraser is not letting a vicious attack from a horse sabotage his rise up the riding ranks.

‌



The 23-year-old was bitten by a rival runner at Ascot earlier this month, leaving a hole in his breeches, and knocked to the ground. But he dusted himself off, remounted Dr Rascal and calmly steered the unbeaten Oliver Cole-trained colt to his second victory.

‌



“Of course it hurt, you saw me rolling on the ground,” said Fraser, recounting the Ascot incident. “It hurt a lot and left a bruise on my thigh. The bruising has gone now and there is a bit of a scar there.

‌



“I was lucky to get up after and ride the winner a couple of minutes later.”

Dr Rascal will be one of the horses Fraser is set to ride at Glorious Goodwood this week, in today’s Vintage Stakes, during what will be the biggest week of his career so far.

The Rebecca Menzies-trained Adonius in the Molecomb Stakes, who has won three on the bounce, is his other stand out mount.

‌



View 3 Images Kaiya Fraser is hauled off his mount as Mr Twig attacks him (Image: At The Races)

“It’s my first time in Group races so I am obviously excited and I am on two unbeaten horses,” he said.

“Obviously they are going to have to step up again in this company and then we can really see how good they are and where they stand in the top company.”

‌



The 23-year-old has followed an untypical path into horse racing, having been born and raised an Eastender, in Hackney, London.

His late grandfather Winston, who loved a bet, piqued his interest in the sport and he gained his first experience of horses from a volunteering stint at the Ebony Horse Club in Brixton.

Aged 16, he enrolled on an apprentice course at the British Racing School in Newmarket, got his first job with the now retired Chris Wall, and now works for Harry Eustace.

‌



View 3 Images Kaiya Fraser: won on Adonius at Chester (Image: PA)

Despite losing his claim last season Fraser is well on course to improve on his best annual score of 45 wins, having shown his preparedness to travel from home in Newmarket to wherever winners can be found

He added: “I ride a lot for Rebecca and had to travel all the way up to Musselburgh to ride him first time out and again second time out.

Article continues below

“Then I went to Chester and now I’ve got the chance to ride him in a big race. That shows that when you put in the work, you get the best out of it.”

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty secures another Commonwealth bronze in 50m breaststroke
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty secures another Commonwealth bronze in 50m breaststroke

Adam Ramsay-Peaty scored a bronze medal in the men's 100m breaststroke earlier this week and the Team GB athlete has managed to follow that up with another medal

View 2 Images Adam Ramsay-Peaty has been competing at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow (Image: Getty Images)

Adam Ramsay-Peaty secured bronze once again in the 50m breaststroke semi finals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games as Sam Williamson claimed glory.

‌



The Brit was quickly up against it after the start but his late charge wasn't enough to see him bag another hold. He finished in 26.94 - 0.44 off the Australian winner, who was able to back up his 100m performance to secure an incredible double in Glasgow.

‌



Michael Houlie secured second as Ramsay-Peaty finished third by just 0.01. Ramsay-Peaty came into the race as defending champion having won gold four years ago in Birmingham and revved up the crowd during his walk-in, but it wasn't enough to inspire him to glory.

‌



He said: "It is quite disappointing in terms of the time and as we know times equal medals. I felt I could have been a little quicker but I need to look at it and see where it is going on because nothing makes sense this week to be honest.

Adam Peaty doubles down on family feud as he shares how he copes with tough times READ MORE :

"I am working way too hard. If those results were how much I am working then they would be a lot better. I need to look at that and adjust course because we are sailing in some rough seas right now and it is not sustainable. I have come back from worse and we will see where we end up."

The goal remains a medal at the Olympics in Los Angeles in 2028 but Ramsay-Peaty insists he's happier in himself than when he was dominating the sport.

‌



He said: "Evolution of the man I guess. I came in 2014 and was a young boy, had no responsibilities and all I cared about was my car. Now I am an older man, married, one kid George and also another on the way. Not even comparable where I am now. I am much much happier and now the performances need to catch up."

View 2 Images Adam Ramsay-Peaty secured bronze in the Men's 100m Breaststroke (Image: Getty Images)

He had booked his place in the final with a time of 26.82 seconds, as he finished behind just South Africa's Houlie in his semi-final.

‌



It comes after the Olympian secured a bronze at the weekend in the 100m breaststroke final, despite going in as the fastest qualifier.

He was beaten by Williamson and Jersey history maker Filip Nowacki. His time - 59.65 seconds - was more than four-tenths slower than his semi-final swim and three seconds off his personal best from seven years ago.

He cut an emotional figure afterwards, but his comments have divided opinion after Ramsay-Peaty claimed he "deserved more" after all his efforts after several years away.

Article continues below

He said: "It took a lot of courage to get back into the sport, so we should be happy with everything we get, but then that contradicts the athlete inside me and what I work for.

"I just think I deserve more. I know sport isn't about what you deserve or even what you work for - it's who gets it on the day. I just know I'm a better athlete than that. It's very disappointing."

Sports.title: Italy in turmoil as legend ready to quit 16 days into job after manager pick blocked
Sports.content:
Italy in turmoil as legend ready to quit 16 days into job after manager pick blocked

Paolo Maldini has reportedly quit as Italy's technical director after just over two weeks in the role following the decision to block Andrea Pirlo from becoming manager

View 2 Images Paolo Maldini has quit his role with Italy

Italy's technical director Paolo Maldini has quit after only 16 days having seen Andrea Pirlo blocked for the vacant manager's role, according to reports.

‌



The Azzurri are on the lookout for a new boss after Gennaro Gattuso quit following another failure to qualify for the World Cup. As part of a huge reset Maldini, who played his entire career at AC Milan and won 126 caps for his country, was hired into a senior role.

‌



He was tasked with restoring Italy to their former glory and the all-time great defender had pushed for Pirlo’s appointment. After seeing that request turned down Sky Italy claim he has now walked away after just over two weeks in his job.

‌



Pirlo, part of the victorious 2006 World Cup side, expressed his frustration at being snubbed with a post on social media. He wrote: "After learning last night that I am no longer the candidate to lead the Italian national team, I believe it is my duty to clarify a few points.

Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

"In the last few days I have witnessed with great bitterness the debate that has developed around my name and the possibility of taking over the role of head coach of the Italian national team.

Pirlo was not allowed to take on the role because of his connections to the Russian betting company Fonbet, where he is a brand ambassador. The former player has said it is “strictly commercial and sporting in nature”. Some involved in the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), as well as politicians, didn't think it was right he took up the post due to the ongoing war in Ukraine.

‌



Pirlo is ultimately the third major name to miss out on the role. Pep Guardiola said no for personal reasons and Carlo Ancelotti didn't want to leave his gig with Brazil.

View 2 Images Andrea Pirlo was overlooked for the role due to ties with Russia (Image: Gabriele Siri/IPA Sport/ipa-agency.net/REX/Shutterstock)

Gattuso resigned in April after Italy’s failure to qualify for this summer’s World Cup. They finished below Norway in qualifying and then lost to Bosnia-Herzegovina on penalties in the play-offs.

Article continues below

It further amplified Italy's decline with the Azzurri now missing out on the 2018, 2022 and 2026 editions. They became the first winner in history to fail to qualify for three tournaments on the bounce as their Euros success of five years ago continues to look like a distant memory.

Italy came into those championships off the back of a sensational unbeaten run and downed the likes of Belgium and Spain before beating England at Wembley in the final. Roberto Mancini was their manager but, despite some high profile men taking the job since, they continue to fall short.

Sports.title: Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing
Sports.content:
Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing

Jordan Henderson is a target for multiple Premier League clubs, with Brentford willing to let him go on a free transfer, and Chelsea are understood to be leading the race for his services

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson is another shock target for Chelsea (Image: Adrian Dennis/AFP via Getty Images)

Chelsea are working on a surprise move for Jordan Henderson, sitting first in the queue of Premier League clubs who are interested in signing him. Henderson, 36, has an agreement which will him to leave Brentford on a free transfer, despite having one year left on his contract.

‌



The midfielder is currently injured after breaking his arm during England's celebrations following their last-16 win against Mexico at the World Cup. Henderson stayed in North America for the rest of the tournament, remaining a key figure within the dressing room.

‌



His leadership and experience are part of why Xabi Alonso wants to bring him to Stamford Bridge. The Athletic report that Chelsea are the leading contenders for the former Liverpool captain's signature.

‌



It's added that multiple Premier League clubs also want to sign him. Chelsea's interest comes after they opened talks with Brighton to sign 35-year-old Danny Welbeck, further proof of their change of transfer policy since Alonso was appointed.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

Last month, the Blues bid £8m for Granit Xhaka after the Sunderland captain signalled that he'd be willing reunite with Alonso, who he played under at Bayer Leverkusen. Sunderland flatly rejected the offer and Xhaka will stay.

‌



Henderson is seen as alternative, with Alonso wanting an experienced head in midfield, while he also gets on well with Chelsea's new £117million signing, Morgan Rogers. The England international only joined Brentford a year ago from Ajax, previously playing for Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq having left Liverpool in July 2023.

But his impact off the pitch is valued, too. After beating France 6-4 in the World Cup third-place play-off, England boss Thomas Tuchel revealed that the 35-year-old had given a powerful speech pre-match speech which motivated his team-mates.

"Jordan Henderson gave a very impressive speech today in the hotel to put this in the right frame and put everyone in the right mindset," Tuchel explained. "So he helped unbelievably today.

‌



Should Jordan Henderson join Chelsea? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson stayed with the England squad, despite breaking his arm (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

"That was very emotional and very, very impressive to put this game into perspective. I won't say what he said, but it puts into it perspective because he was part of this match eight years ago.

‌



"It was very emotional and he put into perspective what you might feel in the very moment, that you might give in to the feeling 'I don't want to be here'. He took all of that away because he said that it means the world in the end, and he would give anything if he hadn't broken his arm to be part again in this match.

"You never know when you get a World Cup match for England. He said it much, much better than me and more emotional, and it was very impressive. He set the tone and the mindset for this match."

Sports.title: Man Utd star takes drastic action as Ruben Amorim plots transfer reunion
Sports.content:
Man Utd star takes drastic action as Ruben Amorim plots transfer reunion

One Manchester United player could be set for a departure from Old Trafford and a reunion with a former boss in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Manchester United star Noussair Mazraoui has been linked with a reunion with Ruben Amorim (Image: (Photo by Hannah Peters - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Manchester United defender Noussair Mazraoui has reportedly switched agents as speculation continues to mount regarding a potential departure from Old Trafford. Reports earlier this summer suggested new AC Milan manager and former United boss Ruben Amorim was interested in reuniting with the Morocco international.

‌



The Serie A outfit is searching for a wing-back to feature in Amorim's favoured 3-4-3 system, with Mazraoui being considered. Italian reports indicate the Serie A side would pursue a deal for the United defender, provided decision-makers at Old Trafford signal their willingness to sell.

‌



Amorim had previously heaped praise on Mazraoui during his Old Trafford tenure, saying: "He’s a top player. He understands the game. He knows how to attack, he’s very technical, he’s very good defensively and he’s very good one-on-one."

‌



There are, however, questions about what position the Moroccan World Cup star would occupy in Amorim's setup, having also featured as a centre-back under the Portuguese manager during his spell at Old Trafford. According to Fabrizio Romano, Mazraoui has joined new agency Panthera, who will handle his representation going forward, though it's unclear whether there's any direct link between that choice and a potential transfer this summer.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

There are, however, questions about what position the Moroccan World Cup star would occupy in Amorim's setup, having also featured as a centre-back under the Portuguese manager during his spell at Old Trafford. According to Fabrizio Romano, Mazraoui has joined new agency Panthera, who will handle his representation going forward, though it's unclear whether there's any direct link between that choice and a potential transfer this summer.

‌



Amorim, speaking in December 2024, added: "He’s a modern player. I think he’s the future of our team. When you think about him, you think we need more players like Nous that can control the tempo, they are really, really good and comfortable with the ball. So, Nous, I’m really happy with him."

The Moroccan defender was a regular for his country as they reached the latter stages of the World Cup, just a few months on from reaching the African Cup of Nations final. The 28-year-old defender made 20 appearances for United last season, sitting out a substantial portion of the campaign for the African Cup of Nations.

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim could raid his former club (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Mazraoui found it difficult to regain his spot in Michael Carrick's team after coming back from the winter competition, but did catch the eye of the then-interim United manager, eventually reclaiming his place in the starting XI.

"Yeah he's come back well, Nous," Carrick said last season after reintegrating Mazraoui back into the side. "It was a difficult one, obviously, on the back of the final and how it panned out.

"[He had] a few days to digest that then back in and around it. He's been fantastic in and around the group and around training.

Article continues below

"Obviously, he came on at the end of the game and played a part for us, as you'd expect. So yeah, again [we want to] just keep thickening the squad, bolstering the squad and it's great to have him back."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
