World.title: Three quarters of Poles support cooperation with Ukraine against Russia despite historical dispute
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A new study shows that, while most Poles were angered by President Volodymyr Zelensky’s recent decision to name a military unit after a group that massacred Poles in World War Two, they still overwhelmingly support cooperation with Ukraine and believe that Russia benefits from the dispute. The study, carried out by Polish state research agency CBOS, also finds that a large majority of Poles believe good relations with Ukraine will only be possible once historical issues are resolved. The polling was carried out this month in response to the ongoing diplomatic crisis that began in May, when Zelensky named a military unit after the “heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA)”. The UPA is widely revered in Ukraine for its role in fighting against Moscow-backed Soviet rule. However, in Poland it is associated with the Volhynia massacres, in which around 100,000 Polish civilians – mostly women and children – were slaughtered during World War Two, often with great brutality. Zelensky’s decision sparked anger in Poland, where the massacres are regarded as a genocide (though Ukraine strongly rejects that label). In June, Polish President Karol Nawrocki stripped Zelensky of the Order of the White Eagle, Poland’s highest honour, which he had received in 2023. In its new survey, CBOS found that 59% of Poles support Nawrocki’s decision, while only 28% oppose it. However, they were divided over the consequences, with 41% saying it would bring Poland more losses than benefits and the exact same proportion saying the benefits would outweigh the costs. More broadly, 84% said the Polish state should react when another country glorifies historical figures responsible for crimes against Poles. However, when asked if Ukrainians have the right to honour their own historical heroes, even if those figures left a negative mark on Polish history, 44% agreed and 42% disagreed. At the same time, over three quarters of respondents (77%) said that good Polish-Ukrainian relations could not be built without addressing the past, but a similar proportion (73%) also believe that politicians on both sides “fuel conflicts between Poles and Ukrainians for their own political gain”. Poland has cautiously welcomed President @ZelenskyyUa's announcement of a five-point plan to alleviate the diplomatic crisis triggered by his earlier decision to name a military unit after a group that led massacres of Poles during WWII https://t.co/M3GXD9vtAr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 18, 2026 Yet the survey also showed that, for Poles, historical disputes have not displaced security concerns, and in particular the view that, for Poland and Ukraine, Russia is a shared enemy. Some 75% of respondents agreed with the statement that “Poland and Ukraine should, above all, cooperate in the face of the threat from Russia, rather than focus on the issues that divide them”. The most frequently cited priorities in relations with Kyiv were security cooperation (61%), building good neighbourly relations (46%), commemorating victims of the Volhynia massacres (43%), strengthening Poland’s regional leadership (41%), and ensuring Polish companies participate in Ukraine’s reconstruction (40%). Just over half of Poles (52%) agree that “Poland and Ukraine have more common aims and interests than conflicting ones”, while 32% disagreed. A huge majority (80%) agreed that “Russia benefits from the Polish-Ukrainian dispute”. W ocenie społecznej zdecydowanym priorytetem w relacjach z Ukrainą powinna być współpraca na rzecz bezpieczeństwa – wskazało ją 61% badanych.📊 ➡️Więcej w komunikacie #CBOS "Wokół polsko-ukraińskiego sporu o imponderabilia i nie tylko":https://t.co/pIvYbu8gyz#Ukraina #relacje pic.twitter.com/LOpmAKNnXn — CBOS (@CBOS_Info) July 23, 2026 Based on the answers in the survey, CBOS identified three broad groups of respondents classified by their views of the dispute. The largest, described as “moralists”, accounted for 46% and placed greater emphasis on historical grievances. Among this group, 99% supported Nawrocki’s decision and said good Polish-Ukrainian relations could not be built without addressing the past. “Pragmatists”, who made up 34% of respondents, placed greater emphasis on future cooperation. Some 96% said Poland and Ukraine should cooperate against the Russian threat rather than focus on historical disputes. The smallest group, labelled by CBOS as “withdrawn”, represented 20% of respondents who were more likely to lack a clear view on Polish-Ukrainian relations. Long-simmering tensions between Poland and Ukraine over WWII massacres have finally boiled over, prompting a diplomatic crisis.@danieltilles1 looks at how we got here and what it may mean for the two countries and Europe more broadly https://t.co/a8tiYJJHRr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 22, 2026 Recent weeks have seen moves from Ukraine towards finding a diplomatic solution to the crisis. In early July, foreign minister Andrii Sybiha visited Warsaw to propose an “anti-crisis package” of measures. Last week, Zelensky himself outlined a five-point plan to alleviate the dispute, including opening up Ukrainian historical archives and permitting more exhumations of victims of the massacres, most of whom remain buried in mass graves in Ukraine. The Polish authorities have cautiously welcomed Zelensky’s announcement, though also emphasise that they are waiting to see concrete action. Meanwhile, there is no indication that Zelensky will change his decision to name a unit after the heroes of the UPA. Keeping dogs and cats chained up at home will be banned in Poland from next year, after President Karol Nawrocki signed into law a bill prohibiting the practice. His decision ends a long-running dispute over the issue, after Nawrocki last year vetoed a previous proposal to ban chaining because it also included what he argued were excessive and unrealistic additional measures on minimum kennel sizes for dogs. Zawetowana w listopadzie 2025 r. ustawa łańcuchowa była źle przygotowana i przeregulowana, ponieważ nakładała na obywateli obowiązki, których wielu nie byłoby w stanie spełnić. Dzisiaj otrzymujemy ustawę lepszą, z pozytywnym głosem takich podmiotów jak rolniczy samorząd.… pic.twitter.com/h7kIAI77KR — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) July 24, 2026 The new law bans owners from tethering dogs and cats at home. Animals must be kept either inside the house, in a fenced garden or, if that is not possible, in a kennel “large enough for the animal to move freely and satisfy its natural needs”. Dogs kept in kennels must be provided with daily exercise outside of it. Dogs and cats can still be put on leashes in certain situations, such as when they are being walked, but also during transport, while participating in shows, performances or training, if they are at vets or groomers, or if they represent a danger to humans or other animals. Those who are found to have violated the new law can be fined between 1,000 and 100,000 zloty (€232-23,166). If they are deemed to have acted with “extreme cruelty”, they can also face a prison sentence of up to five years, reports the Forsal news service. Now that the bill has been signed by Nawrocki, it will be published in the official Journal of Laws (Dziennik Ustaw), after which it goes into force 12 months later. The new measures represent a successful second attempt to introduce a leashing ban. A previous bill was approved by parliament last September. However, in December, Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, announced that he was vetoing it. The president argued that, “although the intention – protecting animals – is just and noble, the law itself was poorly drafted”. In particular, he said that elements introducing minimum sizes for dog kennels were unrealistic and would “harm farmers, breeders and ordinary rural households”. After an attempt by parliament to overturn the veto failed, legislators went back to the drawing board and, following discussions with the president’s chancellery and animal rights groups, drafted a compromise bill that was approved by parliament earlier this month. The bill received support from the current ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, as well as most MPs from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), the main opposition party. The far-right Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) voted against it. Thousands of people have protested in Warsaw against President @NawrockiKn's veto of a law that would have banned the chaining up of dogs Parliament will vote on Wednesday on whether to overturn Nawrocki's veto, which would require a three-fifths majority https://t.co/0GRup2sppb — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 15, 2025 “We now have a better law, with positive feedback from entities such as the agricultural chamber,” said Nawrocki today. “It demonstrates that the pressure of the presidential veto makes sense. My previous decision to refuse to sign this bill forced the government and parliament to work harder.” However, although Nawrocki said the new law would no longer entail “rigid and costly requirements” for kennels, his office noted in a separate statement that the legislation requires the agriculture minister to issue a regulation establishing “minimum kennel area, taking into account the dog’s size”. It remains unclear if and how that would differ from the requirements Nawrocki previously vetoed. The presidential chancellery also noted that the law itself already outlines that kennels must be made of “wood or wood-like material with thermal insulation”, must be insulated from the ground, and must have openings on at least two sides to allow light and air to enter. Police officers and rangers have stepped up joint patrols in Poland’s mountainous Tatra National Park during the peak summer season, following a spate of rule-breaking including swimming in the park’s lakes and ponds, driving cars and going off marked trails. Meanwhile, national park authorities have repeated warnings that bathing, littering and breaking other rules can damage the park’s fragile ecosystem. Local police officers have joined Tatra National Park rangers on patrols on popular tourist routes. On one such patrol last week, officers focused on education and prevention, reminding visitors not to leave marked trails or litter and explaining how to behave safely and responsibly in the mountains. They also checked that organised groups were accompanied by qualified mountain guides, as required by law. Fines for such offences range from 50 zloty (€11.55) to as much as 1,000 zloty (€231) in the event of environmental damage or multiple offences. Police said that all visitors encountered during the patrol were complying with the park’s regulations. However, they added that similar patrols would continue on a regular basis. The Tatra National Park, home to Poland’s highest peaks, and the nearby mountain resort of Zakopane are among the country’s most popular holiday destinations, with crowds taking to park trails in the summer season. The park, the most visited of Poland’s 23 national parks, welcomed a record 5.3 million visitors in 2025 and offers 275 km of marked hiking trails, including high-altitude routes that connect at several points with the adjacent national park in Slovakia. 🚨 Ukraiński Influencer wjechał nielegalnie samochodem na Morskie oko 🗣️: Jesteśmy pierwszymi ludźmi w historii, którzy wjechali samochodem nad Morskie Oko. As a result, he was banned from entering Poland and other Schengen Area countries for five years. Tourists have also been filmed entering Morskie Oko and other protected lakes and ponds, which is not permitted in the national park. This month, a group of young Dutch tourists were filmed bathing in Przedni Staw Polski in the Valley of the Five Lakes, one of the Tatras’ best-known hiking destinations. World.title: Polish opposition PiS party set to split, with over 30 MPs being expelled
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. More than 30 MPs from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s main opposition party, have effectively resigned after refusing to sign a loyalty pledge, party leader Jarosław Kaczyński has announced. The dispute centres around a more moderate faction in the party aligned with former prime minister and deputy PiS leader Mateusz Morawiecki, who is one of those now set to be expelled from the party. They have for months been unhappy with PiS’s move in a hard-right direction. 💬 Prezes PiS Jarosław Kaczyński @OficjalnyJK. 👉 Udostępnij pic.twitter.com/bycjE0Yq0f — Prawo i Sprawiedliwość (@pisorgpl) July 24, 2026 “Around 30-something…of our group’s MPs have resigned,” revealed Kaczyński at a press conference on Friday. He added that their departures would be formalised at a meeting of the party’s political committee scheduled for Tuesday next week. Kaczyński’s announcement came after a deadline expired at midnight on Thursday for its MPs to sign a pledge of loyalty to the party that included a commitment not to be members of any external political associations. That measure was aimed in particular at an association called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) founded by Morawiecki in April. The former prime minister had always insisted that his organisation was intended as complementary to PiS, rather than a rival to it. However, many figures in the party saw it as an attempt by Morawiecki to create a separate centre of power, and potentially to use the association as a launchpad for creating his own party ahead of the autumn 2027 parliamentary elections. The right-wing opposition PiS party has threatened disciplinary action, including exclusion from electoral lists, against dozens of its MPs who have joined a new internal group led by former PM @MorawieckiM and intended to appeal to more moderate voters https://t.co/y62Cm361U2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 17, 2026 After PiS issued a resolution on Wednesday last week requiring that its parliamentarians pledge to withdraw from any such associations, most of its 186 MPs quickly complied. However, a group of between 30 and 40 who are part of Development Plus refused to do so. “Everyone knew what they were supposed to sign, and knew the consequences of not signing,” said Kaczyński on Friday. “And so they made the decision they did.” “In this situation, we cannot view the [Development Plus] association as anything other than a component of a plan…to split our party,” he added. However, although its supporters will now leave PiS, “we want to part ways without any animosity”, said Kaczyński. After Kaczyński’s announcement, senior figures from Development Plus made clear that no one from their association had resigned from PiS. They had simply not signed the declaration of loyalty demanded by the party. Later, Morawiecki himself held a press conference in parliament surrounded by his supporters. He claimed that an unnamed “small group of schemers” within PiS had been seeking to turn Kaczyński against him and push him out of the party. “We fought for the unity of Law and Justice until the very end,” declared Morawiecki, who said that his group included 40 MPs, one senator and three MEPs. However, three of the MPs are not members of PiS, and therefore were not expected to sign the loyalty declaration. Szanowni Państwo! 🟦Do ostatniej chwili walczyłem o jedność Prawa i Sprawiedliwości. Nie o stanowiska. Nie o osobiste ambicje. Nie o wpływy. 🟦Walczyłem o jedność obozu, który przez osiem lat zmieniał Polskę – budował jej bezpieczeństwo, rozwijał gospodarkę i przywracał godność… pic.twitter.com/PP7sOkzMHp — Mateusz Morawiecki (@MorawieckiM) July 24, 2026 If the expulsion of Morawiecki’s supporters is confirmed, it will mark a major shake-up of Poland’s political landscape. PiS has for the last two decades been the dominant force on the Polish right, including periods leading governments in 2005-2007 and 2015-2023. However, since losing power at elections in 2023, when the party won 35% of the vote, PiS has seen its average support in polls fall to around 23-24%, the lowest level in 14 years. Meanwhile, it has been challenged by the rise of the far right, where two parties, Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), now together poll a similar combined level of support to PiS. In response, Kaczyński in March named a hardline figure, Przemyszław Czarnek, as PiS’s candidate for prime minister in next year’s elections. Czarnek was seen as someone who could appeal to far-right voters, while also potentially working with the far right if a coalition was needed after the elections. Support for PiS has fallen to its lowest in 14 years, as the party grapples with internal division, the rise of far-right challengers, living in President Nawrocki's shadow, and the unpopularity in Poland of PiS ally Donald Trump, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/QRScBpEQQG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 2, 2026 However, there has been no rise in support for PiS since Czarnek was named, prompting growing concern from more moderate figures within the party, led by Morawiecki. They argue that PiS has wrongly disowned many of the successes of its time in office before 2023, and they fear that its rightward shift damages its chances of winning over more centrist voters. Morawiecki, who was an international banker before joining PiS to become finance minister and then prime minister, wants the party to focus on more technocratic issues, such as economic development, rather than Euroscepticism and culture wars. That has led to frequent public sparring between his supporters and others in the party. In April, PiS threatened disciplinary action against members of Development Plus. Kaczyński and Morawiecki then reached an agreement that allowed the association to continue. But that uneasy truce has now fallen apart. World.title: Not an Official Visit: Petr Pavel Attends Hungarian GP as F1 Photographer
World.content:
The president of the Czech Republic, Petr Pavel, has made his way to the Formula 1 Hungarian Grand Prix on Sunday – but was not an official visit.

Ever wondered what world leaders do in their free time? For Czech Republic president Petr Pavel, the answer is sports photography – and he’s particularly passionate about motorsport.

This weekend, he was attending the Hungarian GP with a full photography kit – and an official FIA accreditation. He arrived at the Hungaroring for Saturday’s sessions and was already taking pictures, accompanied by Czech F1 photographer Jiri Krenek.



This wasn’t the first time he was seen at a major motorsport event as a hobby photographer. Most recently, Pavel travelled to France in June to attend the Le Mans 24 Hours, once again equipped with full camera gear.

In fact, the former NATO Military Chairman has attended several races on both two and four wheels over the years.

Within the Czech Republic, Pavel covered the MotoGP and World Superbike events at Brno, while he has travelled as far as the US and Saudi Arabia to photograph NASCAR and the Dakar Rally respectively.

Last year, he also raised nearly 30,000 euros for a charity dedicated to children, single parents and the elderly by auctioning a photo album.

While it is unusual for politicians to attend races purely for leisure, several leaders regularly appear at major motorsport events in their own countries.

Last year, then British Prime Minister Keir Starmer hosted F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali, drivers and senior team figures at a reception in 10 Downing Street ahead of the British GP.

World.title: Best Petting Zoos in Prague for Families with Kids (2026 Guide)
World.content:
Prague Zoo gets all the attention — and fair enough, it’s consistently ranked among the top zoos in the world — but the city is also full of smaller, low-key spots where kids can get hands-on with animals.

These mini farms and forest parks are perfect for a relaxed weekend outing, most are free or nearly free, and several are just a short metro ride from the centre.

Here’s our pick of the best small zoos and petting farms around Prague.

1. Milíčovský dvůr – Prague 11

Right on the edge of Milíčov forest, this outdoor farm is home to a horse, an ostrich, a fox, goats, sheep, pigs, rabbits and more. Feed dispensers let kids feed the animals directly, and there’s a sandpit, a wooden playground and a small snack stand on site. Entry costs just 20 CZK. Closed Mondays.

📍 K Milíčovu 100/8, Prague 11 — nearest metro: Háje



2. Chuchle Grove Mini Zoo – Prague 5

Set on a hillside inside the Chuchle Grove nature park, this zoo run by Prague’s city forestry service cares for injured and orphaned wildlife. Expect to see mouflons, deer, wild boar, owls, lynxes and more — though petting isn’t allowed here, since the focus is conservation and education. Free entry, open 24/7, with a playground and refreshment kiosk nearby

📍 V Lázních 8, Prague 5

3. Station of Young Biologists – Prague 5

A mix of indoor and outdoor spaces near Anděl, with a tropical terrarium (crocodiles, monkeys, boas), an aviary, and outdoor pens with kangaroos, llamas, ponies and goats. Regular workshops and interactive shows run alongside the animal exhibits. General entry is free; the terrarium and greenhouses cost a small fee (20–40 CZK).

📍 Drtinova 1A, Prague 5 — near Anděl metro

4. Toulcův dvůr – Prague 10

An 8.5-hectare environmental education centre in Hostivař with cows, horses, chickens, pigs, sheep and goats, plus a cherry orchard, wetlands and a farm-to-table restaurant. Petting and feeding aren’t permitted, but it’s a beautifully kept site for a nature walk.

📍 Kubátova 1/32, Prague 10

Honourable mentions

If you’re just after a nice walk with a chance of spotting animals, these free spots are worth a detour:

Wild Garden Hostivař (Prague 15) — rare white fallow deer and mouflons roam near a flooded quarry, with a playground and lakeside walk.

(Prague 15) — rare white fallow deer and mouflons roam near a flooded quarry, with a playground and lakeside walk. Kunratice Forest (Prague 4) — sheep, dwarf goats and pigs can be fed at the “Na tý louce zelený” restaurant, with spotted deer and mouflons visible along the trails.

(Prague 4) — sheep, dwarf goats and pigs can be fed at the “Na tý louce zelený” restaurant, with spotted deer and mouflons visible along the trails. Kamýk Forest (Prague 12) — a small goat enclosure and pheasant aviary tucked next to the gamekeeper’s lodge, surrounded by walking and cycling trails.

World.title: Stromovka: A Green Paradise in the Heart of Prague
World.content:
Stromovka is one of the largest and most popular parks in Prague, drawing visitors with its beautiful nature, rich history, and numerous activities.

Let’s explore what Stromovka offers and how to get there.

Why Visit Stromovka?

Looking for a break from the city’s hustle and bustle or the perfect spot for a picnic with friends? Stromovka is your ideal choice. This vast park features green meadows, shady alleys, and ample opportunities for sports and cultural events.

What is Stromovka?

Stromovka, officially known as Královská obora, spans more than 95 hectares, making it one of Prague’s largest green spaces. Located in Prague 7, the park is a favorite among joggers, cyclists, families, and anyone looking to escape into nature without leaving the city.

It’s perfect for walks, picnics, sports, or simply relaxing on the grass.



A Brief History

Stromovka’s history dates back to the 13th century when it was established as a royal hunting ground. Over time, it evolved and expanded, becoming a public park in the 19th century. The park is home to the original Vltava Creek and several ponds, which host various water birds.

Throughout its history, Stromovka has undergone many changes, shaping it into the popular relaxation spot it is today.

Activities in Stromovka

Stromovka offers a wide range of activities for all ages. Here are some ideas:

Walking and Running: Enjoy the scenic trails.

Cycling: Explore the park on two wheels.

Picnics: Large meadows and shady spots are perfect for a picnic.

Sports: Play football, volleyball, and other sports.

Cultural Events: Attend various events hosted in the park.

How to Get to Stromovka

By Metro: The nearest metro station is Nádraží Holešovice (line C). From there, it’s just a few minutes’ walk to Stromovka.

By Tram: Trams also reach the park. The nearest stops are Výstaviště Holešovice (lines 6, 12, 17) and Planetarium Prague (line 6).

By Bike: Cycling enthusiasts can easily access Stromovka by bike. Bike-sharing stations like Rekola and Nextbike are available around the park, allowing you to ride directly into this natural haven.

World.title: August 12-31: Prague to Host Festival of New Circus Letní Letná
World.content:
The international festival of new circus and theatre, Letní Letná 2026, will take place in Prague on August 12-31.

The festival will feature over 200 performances, workshops, concerts, and various acts by circus artists from 14 countries, including a special program for children.

This year marks the 23rd edition of the festival. Letenské sady park will once again be the main venue, with tents set up to create a mini-town complete with a coffee shop and an evening bar.



Many performances will be free of charge. Additionally, the festival will offer a rich and varied daily program: children’s shows, circus, juggling and acrobat workshops, music concerts, exhibitions, lectures, creative workshops, and more.

One of this year’s highlights is Wolf by Australia’s renowned Circa ensemble. The international lineup also includes Switzerland’s Accademia Teatro Dimitri, presenting its graduate production La Grinta, and Seismic, a collaboration between French choreographer Marie Gourdain and German artist Felix Baumann, featuring Czech performers.

The Czech program includes the premiere of Vertige by AirGym Art Company, Enola by Eliška Brtnická, new productions from Losers Cirque Company, and Hey, Earth! by Cirque La Putyka.

Emerging talent will also take center stage, with performances by CZirkidz Dance Company, Teens Cirkabaret, and recent graduates of international circus schools.

Audiences will have the chance to experience works in progress, including K voknu by Michaela Stará and Filip Zahradnický, followed by discussions with the artists.

For adults, Světla a stíny by Silk&Steel explores the darker sides of human experience through aerial and ground acrobatics, while family-friendly performances include the popular (Not Only) Juggling Galashow and Orbiting Zero by Czech juggler Aleš Hrdlička.

Beyond the performances, visitors can enjoy free workshops, children’s activities, concerts, open-air events, food stalls, bars, and relaxation areas throughout the festival grounds. Babysitting is available during selected performances, and the venue is fully accessible, making Letní Letná a festival for all ages.

World.title: New Railway Tunnel to Cut Prague to Pilsen Journey to 45 Minutes
World.content:
The Czech government has approved the next phase of one of its largest railway infrastructure projects: a new tunnel connecting Prague and Beroun.

Construction is expected to begin in 2032, with completion scheduled for 2044.

The 24.7-kilometre double-track tunnel will significantly shorten travel times on one of the country’s busiest rail corridors.

Once completed, trains will travel between Prague-Smíchov station and Beroun in around 13 minutes, reducing the current journey time by more than 30 minutes.

The project will also improve connections towards western Czechia and neighbouring Germany. The journey from Prague to Pilsen is expected to take approximately 45 minutes, while international rail services to Munich and Nuremberg will become faster and more reliable.



New railway line designed for speeds of up to 200 km/h

The planned railway route will include a new high-speed section designed for trains travelling at up to 200 km/h. The tunnel will begin near Prague-Smíchov station, pass beneath the Barrandov area, and emerge near Beroun.

A separate connection on the Prague side is also planned, linking the new line with Braník Bridge and Prague-Krč. The additional infrastructure will improve connections within the capital while increasing capacity on the wider railway network.

Construction preparation underway

Preparatory work for the tunnel is already in progress. Geological surveys and technical documentation are currently being completed, with the application for a construction permit expected to be submitted between 2028 and 2029.

After the approval process, Správa železnic will launch a tender to select the construction company responsible for building the tunnel.

The Czech Railway Administration estimates the total cost of the project will continue to rise due to inflation and increasing construction expenses. However, its director general Tomáš Tóth said the estimated cost of around CZK 3 billion per kilometre remains comparable with similar railway tunnel projects abroad.

The project is expected to increase railway capacity towards western Czechia, improve timetable reliability, and strengthen connections between Prague, Pilsen, and major German cities.

World.title: Thailand Brings Its Culture and Flavours to Prague at Thai Market 2026
World.content:
The colours, flavours, and warm spirit of Thailand return to the capital on Friday, 4 September 2026, as the Royal Thai Embassy proudly hosts Thai Market 2026 at the historic Písecká brána.

Organised alongside Team Thailand—comprising the Thai Trade Centre and the Tourism Authority of Thailand in Prague—this year’s flagship event is held in active cooperation with the Prague 6 Municipality.

More info on Facebook here.

“Thai Market has become a meaningful platform to bring Thailand closer to the Czech public through friendship, creativity, and people-to-people connections,” said H.E. Mr. Pichit Boonsud, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Thailand to the Czech Republic.

“This year, we are thrilled to celebrate Prague 6 Day with our Thai Market to show our true partnership with the local municipality. This event is a heartfelt cultural exchange and our way of actively engaging with the wonderful community that hosts us.”



Open to all ages with free admission, the event will offer a full day of authentic Thai experiences, from traditional cuisine and refreshing drinks such as Thai iced tea to popular desserts including Mango Sticky Rice and Thai tea ice cream.

The programme will also feature live stage performances, premium Thai products from Czech importers, traditional Thai massages, and activities where guests can win vouchers to spend at the event.

A dedicated tourism section will provide inspiration and information for those planning their next trip to Thailand. Thai Market 2026 promises to be a vibrant celebration of Thai culture, flavours, and community in the heart of Prague.

World.title: Future of Prague’s Výtoň Bridge Could Be Decided by the End of This Year
World.content:
The Railway Administration (Správa železnic) is expected to decide on the future design of Prague’s Výtoň Railway Bridge by the end of this year.

If the final plan is approved, construction could begin in 2028.

The long-delayed project has become the centre of a dispute between transport authorities and heritage experts. While railway officials argue that a new three-track structure is necessary to meet future transport demands, conservationists continue to push for the preservation of the existing historic bridge.

The Railway Administration has warned that the current condition of the bridge requires a final decision soon.

Dispute over historic structure

The main proposal currently under consideration is the construction of a new three-track railway bridge. Správa železnic selected a project team last year, but the plan remains controversial due to opposition from heritage authorities and groups seeking to preserve the original structure.

The debate has also attracted international attention. UNESCO representatives are preparing a Heritage Impact Assessment (HIA), which will examine how the planned changes could affect Prague’s cultural heritage.

The Transport Association supports the construction of a new bridge, arguing that rebuilding the existing structure would be more expensive and would not provide enough additional capacity.

Construction could start in 2028

According to earlier plans from Správa železnic, work on the project was originally expected to begin sooner. A tender process was completed in 2025, with companies SUDOP Praha and TOP CON SERVIS selected for the preparation of the three-track bridge project.

The estimated cost of the entire project is around CZK 3.4 billion.

Because of the bridge’s deteriorating condition, trains currently operate on only one track and must reduce speed when crossing the structure. The construction of the additional third track alone is expected to cost approximately CZK 129 million.

World.title: Prague Compared to 11 European Cities: Housing, Jobs, Transport,
World.content:
A new report from the Prague Institute of Planning and Development (IPR) compares life in Prague with 11 other European cities, following a typical resident’s day—from housing and commuting to work, education, and leisure.

Based on verified data collected directly from partner cities, the study highlights both Prague’s strengths and its biggest challenges.

Prague Has Some of Europe’s Least Affordable Housing

The report found that Prague has the least affordable owner-occupied housing among the cities compared.

Buying an apartment requires more than 13 years of gross salary, placing Prague alongside cities such as Barcelona, Munich, and Amsterdam. Unlike many Western European cities, Prague also lacks relatively affordable rental housing.

Renting a 60-square-meter apartment costs around 40% of the average salary in Prague. By comparison, the same apartment would consume about 28% of average income in Munich and just 14% in Vienna.

Strong Job Market, But Lower Incomes

Prague continues to have one of the lowest unemployment rates in Europe, making it relatively easy to find work.

However, real incomes remain below those of most Western European capitals. Workers in Munich earn roughly 50% more than those in Prague, while wages in cities such as Copenhagen have grown steadily over the past decade.

Although Prague residents now work fewer hours than they did ten years ago—less than 39 hours per week on average—they still work around three hours more each week than people in many Western European cities.

Public Transport Is One of Prague’s Biggest Strengths

Prague ranks among Europe’s top cities for public transport.

Around 70% of residents use public transport regularly, while 87% report being satisfied with the service. The city’s extensive tram, metro, and rail networks make commuting easy, and the system stands out for its reliability, dense coverage, and affordability.

A monthly public transport pass costs less than 1% of the average monthly income, making Prague one of the most affordable cities for public transport after Barcelona.

Car Ownership Continues to Rise

Despite having one of Europe’s best public transport systems, Prague continues to see a steady increase in car ownership.

Together with Warsaw and Bucharest, Prague is one of the few cities in the study where the number of registered cars is still growing significantly. By contrast, cities such as Stockholm, Copenhagen, and Vienna have between one-third and one-half fewer cars per capita and a much higher share of electric and hybrid vehicles.

The report warns that increasing car ownership contributes to traffic congestion, road accidents, poorer air quality, and greater pressure on public space.

World.title: PM Péter Magyar: Tisza Party hits the road again, new campaign begins?
World.content:
The Tisza Party does not intend to distance itself from the people after its election victory and will hit the road again, travelling across the country, the prime minister said in a speech before the start of Monday’s parliamentary session.

Citing recent survey figures, Magyar said his party now has some 4.5 million active supporters, adding that no party had enjoyed such a broad base of support since the change of system 36 years ago. He added that people had placed enormous trust in Tisza, but this also entailed enormous responsibility to ensure the party did not distance itself from the people and listened to them after Tisza’s election victory.

The prime minister said the nationwide tour will take them back to the smallest settlements, markets, railway stations, squares, and streets, where they will report on their work, listen to complaints about where the state is failing, and work with the people to define the tasks ahead.

Magyar urged Tisza Island members to prepare for joint work. Referring to the party’s grassroots organisations, he said: “We started with the Tisza Islands, we won together on April 12, and building a functional and humane Hungary can only succeed with them, with those millions of Hungarian people,” he said.

Interim President Forsthoffer: Sándor Palace to reopen for visits

The presidential Sandor Palace will reopen to visitors from 1 to 8 August, the speaker of parliament, exercising the powers of the president, announced on Monday on her Facebook page. Agnes Forsthoffer wrote that the building has “not only a romantic past but also a present rooted in its historical significance”, and encouraged visitors to explore the palace’s representative rooms with a guided tour. Visitors will also hear special chapters from the palace’s 220-year history, she added.

She noted that registration for the Open Doors programme series is available on the Sándor Palace website.

Registered visitors can tour the building’s representative rooms in early classicist style and get acquainted with its history, including the mysterious Roman sarcophagus, the enigmatic death of Prime Minister Pál Teleki, the behind-the-scenes secrets of the salons, and the mystical additional meanings of the furniture and statues, according to the website.

The programme is open to individual visitors or groups of up to 20 people (or 30 on August 8). If a registered group is smaller, it may be combined with other groups or individual visitors for the same tour, it added.

Goal to build ‘truly functional, humane’ country

The government is working to complete the ruling Tisza Party’s commitments to building “a truly functional and humane Hungary” in which “the everyday security, livelihood, and dignity” of citizens are ensured, PM Magyar said ahead of the agenda in parliament on Monday.

Concerning the government’s measures, the prime minister said VAT on prescription medications will be eliminated from Sept 1, adding that “there is no household in Hungary that the move will not affect.” Some 4 million people in Hungary regularly take prescription drugs “and many have been in a situation in which they had no money to buy the prescribed product.”

Turning point in the polls: Orbán may welcome latest survey — are voters really punishing Péter Magyar?

Meanwhile, he said the government had launched a programme to assist some 400,000 children with a school-start aid of 100,000 forint (EUR 277) each. The government will also reduce VAT on firewood from 27 percent to 5 percent, because families heating their homes with wood were “left out of the previous government’s household utility price cap scheme“, the prime minister said.

“These measures are aimed at eliminating the injustice of oligarchs in the middle of Europe getting rich on the money snatched away from millions of Hungarians,” Magyar said.

Orbán government promised Chinese BYD vast subsidies and influx of thousands of guest workers

World.title: Orbán government promised Chinese BYD vast subsidies and influx of thousands of guest workers
World.content:
Hungary’s previous government pledged substantial financial support for BYD’s planned investment in Szeged, a parliamentary state secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has said in a video posted on Facebook on Monday.

‘Guest workers and generous subsidies’

György László Velkey stated that, according to documents held by the ministry, the Hungarian state committed more than 70 billion forints in infrastructure support for the area where BYD is set to establish operations. In addition, the government offered significant direct financial assistance to the company, although the precise sum remains a commercial secret.

Former PM Orbán with the head of the BYD, Wang Chuanfu, in Budapest. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

“I can say, however, that the scale is comparable to the funding provided for the CATL factory in Debrecen,” the state secretary noted, according to MTI.

It also emerged that BYD has been granted permission to bring in around 10,000 guest workers—almost as many as the number of jobs the investment is expected to create, he added.

Inside a BYD car. Photo: FB/Orbán

Talks with BYD leadership

Péter Stumpf, parliamentary state secretary at the Ministry for Rural and Regional Development and MP for the area, said in the same video that residents of Szeged have three key expectations regarding the project.

They expect the company to comply fully with existing legislation—particularly environmental regulations—so as not to endanger public health; to provide well-paid jobs for local residents and Hungarian workers; and to ensure that Szeged benefits from the company’s economic success.

“It appears that Péter Szijjártó, the former minister for foreign affairs and trade, and Fidesz did not represent these interests during the negotiations,” Stumpf said.

Revealed: How Russian intelligence recruits Hungarian youth – and gets away with it

Mr Velkey concluded by stressing that the current government would negotiate with the Chinese company—and with all foreign partners—solely with the interests of Szeged’s residents and the Hungarian people in mind.

Szeged Mayor László Botka at the BYD construction site in 2024. Photo: FB/László Botka

Former foreign minister joins BYD

Mr Szijjártó recently announced that he would resign his parliamentary seat and join BYD as an international executive responsible for global external relations and the development of new business divisions.

The former minister, who has been attending a world championship event in the United States, described his new contract on Facebook as “the signing of the year”. However, many—even within Fidesz—have reportedly viewed the move as a betrayal at a difficult time for the political community.

World.title: Middle Eastern airline resumes Budapest flights earlier than expected
World.content:
Flydubai is to resume its direct flights to Budapest from July 31, the airline announced on Monday in a statement to Hungary’s state news agency MTI.

The carrier said the route would restore a direct air link between Hungary and the United Arab Emirates, offering seamless access to Dubai as well as to its global network of more than 120 destinations. In June, when the company decided to cancel all flights they talked about an August restart.

Flights between Budapest and Dubai will operate three times a week — on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays — from July 31. The frequency is set to increase to a daily service from October 25, 2026.

Since its launch in 2009, flydubai has carried more than 137 million passengers. The airline currently operates a fleet of 97 Boeing 737 aircraft, the Hungarian news agency wrote.

World.title: World’s third public statue of Freddie Mercury unveiled on Lake Balaton – but it bears a striking resemblance to a Hungarian poet
World.content:
The first public statue of Queen legend Freddie Mercury in Hungary has been unveiled on the shores of Lake Balaton, in what is – somewhat surprisingly – only the third such monument in the world.

The statue was inaugurated on Saturday evening in Balatonszemes, a lakeside town that has hosted an annual Queen fan camp for the past 32 years, organised by the Queen Fan Club Cultural Association – making the choice of location a natural one. More curious, however, is the observation that the sculpture bears a remarkable likeness to a celebrated Hungarian poet.

According to a report by Blikk, the project was realised as a joint venture between the association and the local council. Among the guests at the unveiling was Peter Freestone, Mercury’s former personal assistant. The rights to Mercury’s name and legacy, currently managed by Sony Music, were also formally cleared for the statue in an official letter.

“This is my second visit to this wonderful place, where I have once again been able to meet Hungarian Queen fans in person,” said Freestone, who spent 12 years as Mercury’s assistant, close friend and confidant. He first visited Hungary for an exhibition in Budapest. He added that he appreciated the artist’s decision to depict not the flamboyant performer on stage, but a more reflective and quietly brilliant figure.

This year will mark the 33rd Queen camp in Balatonszemes, commemorating both what would have been Mercury’s 80th birthday on 5 September 2026 and Queen’s legendary 1986 concert in Budapest.

As for the Hungarian poet many believe is echoed in the statue’s features, the answer is Attila József.

One thing, however, is certain: in 1986, Freddie Mercury even sang in Hungarian – and the footage still survives.

World.title: Revealed: How Russian intelligence recruits Hungarian youth – and gets away with it
World.content:
A third secretary of the Russian Embassy in Budapest believed to be serving as an agent of Russia’s SVR intelligence agency remains posted in Budapest, despite allegedly attempting to place at least one Hungarian young person into a senior government position in order to extract sensitive information for Moscow.

The case sheds light on how Russian services have sought to build their own espionage networks in Hungary, including during the years of Viktor Orbán’s governments — and how only weakly these efforts have been countered by the Hungarian state. Whether this will change remains an open question.

Russia did not relent under ‘friendly’ Orbán governments

Even after Russia’s attempted invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and throughout the protracted war that followed, successive Orbán governments have struck a conspicuously understanding tone towards Vladimir Putin’s regime. Officially, this has been justified by Hungary’s heavy reliance on Russian energy supplies, making the maintenance of cordial relations a matter of national interest.

Former PM Orbán last year in Moscow with President Putin. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

At times, government rhetoric has also hinted — albeit vaguely — that some of Putin’s criticisms of the West and its eastward expansion are not without merit.

Yet despite this relationship, widely viewed in Brussels as unusually close and politically costly within the EU, Russian intelligence activity in Hungary has not abated. One such operation appears to have failed rather spectacularly — though its alleged organiser continues to work undisturbed at the Russian embassy in Budapest.

The Russian embassy in Budapest’s city centre, near the Andrássy Avenue. Photo: FB/Russian embassy in Budapest

The case offers a stark warning to ambitious young Hungarians tempted by seemingly “irresistible” invitations to travel to Russia.

Talent-spotters target Hungarian youth

Russia’s efforts extend well beyond military force and drone warfare. The Kremlin continues to deploy soft power with intent, including language-study trips, cultural programmes, and international events such as the World Youth Festival held in Sochi in March 2024.

A Hungarian delegation attended the festival, led by Roland B., a Hungarian national living in Russia. Officially an entrepreneur, he is described by Telex as acting in a talent-spotting role — identifying individuals who could later prove useful to Russian intelligence.

It was at this event that Alexander V., the Budapest-based diplomat believed to be linked to the SVR, was introduced — via Roland B. — to a Hungarian applicant for a senior public administration post. The role required national security clearance. Although the candidate allegedly attempted, on instruction, to conceal his contact with Alexander V., the connection was uncovered, and he was denied the position.

Putin again suggests Hungary could regain territory from Ukraine: what he may have meant

Soft power operations continue unhindered

It remains unclear how many Hungarians — young or otherwise — have taken part in similar trips. Participants may find their digital devices accessed, their activities monitored, or themselves placed in compromising situations at informal social events, potentially rendering them vulnerable to coercion or recruitment.

Such gatherings often involve loosely structured programmes, where attendees cannot be certain whether they are speaking to fellow participants or intelligence operatives. According to Telex, even those who do not become agents may still serve a purpose: speaking positively about Russia online or acting as informal advocates for its interests.

Both B. Roland and Alexander V. remain active and are reportedly organising another major event in Yekaterinburg this September, which is again expected to attract numerous Hungarian participants. Roland B. refused to respond to Telex’s questions concerning the issue.

World.title: FM Anita Orbán received bipartisan US Congress delegation in the Hungarian Parliament – photos

A bipartisan delegation from the United States Congress was received at the Hungarian Parliament on Monday by Foreign Minister Anita Orbán, with talks focusing on defence and economic cooperation.

World.title: Another brutal heat dome arrives as Danube nears record low — what to expect this week
World.content:
A weak cold front on Monday will offer little in the way of relief, with searing heat set to return in the second half of the week. Barely has the previous heat dome passed than, according to HungaroMet, several days of peak temperatures between 33C and 38C are again on the cards. Meanwhile, a prolonged lack of rainfall could push the Danube in Budapest to historic lows, disrupting river traffic and deepening drought conditions across Hungary and much of Europe.

New heat dome to follow ‘dry cold front’

HungaroMet forecasts that a weak cold front will cross the country on Monday, bringing cloudier skies in the first half of the day, along with scattered light rain, showers or thunderstorms — mainly east of the Danube, later shifting to the north-east. North-westerly winds may strengthen widely, with gusts turning gale-force in the vicinity of storms. Daytime highs are expected to reach between 29C and 33C, MTI wrote.

Any respite, however, will be short-lived. By Tuesday, sunny spells with fair-weather cloud are expected, with only isolated showers possible in the east. Afternoon temperatures will range between 25C and 32C.

Another brutal heatwave approaches. Photo: Facebook/MÁV-csoport

From Wednesday onwards, clear and dry conditions will increasingly dominate. Highs of 28C to 34C are forecast for Wednesday, rising to 30C to 36C by Thursday. From Friday, a new heat dome is set to develop: temperatures could climb to between 33C and 38C on Friday and Saturday, with local readings of up to 39C possible by Sunday. Nights will bring diminishing relief, with minimum temperatures rising to between 17C and 24C by the weekend.

Danube in Budapest may fall to historic low

The prolonged dry spell is already being reflected in river levels. According to the National Hydrological Forecasting Service, the Danube at Budapest could fall to just 35 centimetres on Tuesday. Given a margin of error of plus or minus 7 centimetres, there is a realistic chance that the current record low could be broken.

The lowest level ever recorded in Budapest was 33 centimetres, measured on 25 October 2018 — though that record had already surpassed a benchmark that had stood since 1947.

The water level of the Danube in Budapest is extreme low. Photo: Facebook/Fővárosi Vízművek

Conditions are unlikely to improve in the near term. Little to no significant rainfall is expected across the Danube’s catchment area over the next six days, leaving scant hope for any meaningful rise in water levels. The low water has already caused serious disruption to shipping: both cargo and passenger vessels have been unable to proceed along several stretches of the river, while restrictions have been introduced in Budapest. Near Komárom, river cruise ships have recently been forced to queue, with passengers transferred to the capital by bus.

Persistently low water levels could, in the longer term, threaten drinking water supplies drawn from the Danube, although no such issues arose during the late-June heatwave, and Budapest Waterworks has issued reassuring statements on the matter.

If you missed: Hungary gripped by alarming drought as iconic lakes and rivers face unprecedented peril

Drought set to intensify

While Monday’s cold front may briefly temper the heat, it will do little to alleviate the lack of rainfall. High-pressure conditions are expected to reassert themselves thereafter, suppressing cloud formation and ensuring continued dry, sunny weather through the rest of the week, Portfólió wrote.

Hungarian agriculture must adapt to the changing weather conditions. Photo: depositphotos.com

Any showers that do develop on Monday will fall well short of replenishing parched soils. HungaroMet’s weekly precipitation anomaly map suggests that not only the Carpathian Basin but much of Europe is likely to receive below-average rainfall for this time of year. A particularly extensive dry zone is emerging across Central and Eastern Europe, pointing to a process on a continental scale.

All signs indicate that drought conditions will deepen in the coming days. The sustained rainfall deficit is placing increasing strain on vegetation, agriculture and water resources, with forecasts offering little indication of prolonged or substantial rainfall in the near future.

World.title: How could a 14-year-old girl fall from the roof of a children’s home? Internal probe and police investigation began
World.content:
Local police are conducting an investigation and the institution has launched an internal probe into the case of a 14-year-old girl who fell from the roof of a children’s home in Pécs (Southwest Hungary) earlier this month, police and the Directorate General for Social Affairs and Child Protection (SZGYF) told MTI on Monday.

14-year-old girl on the roof of the children’s home

The incident was first reported by Telex.hu news portal on Sunday. The SZGYF said the girl was returned to the institution by police officers late on July 11 after she had been absent without permission for more than ten days. As it later turned out, the girl removed the screws securing the safety chains of the skylight of a kitchen and climbed out onto the roof of the building, MTI wrote.

By this time, a staff member of the children’s home had noticed the girl’s disappearance, but since she could not find her in the building, she asked for help from police officers. One of the residents reported seeing someone on the roof, prompting police to alert paramedics and begin a search of the surrounding area. It was during this sweep that they discovered a girl lying on the ground. She was treated at the scene before being taken to hospital, while officers carried out an on-site investigation.

According to the Directorate-General, an internal inquiry into the circumstances remains under way. The Baranya County Police Headquarters told MTI that the Pécs Police Department is examining the case במסגרת criminal proceedings.

The Directorate-General noted that standard upper-floor windows at the home had already been secured against opening prior to the incident. The girl was able to escape only after breaking a safety chain. As an immediate measure, a non-removable fixing has now been installed on the window, while a specialist will implement a permanent solution using a bespoke fastening method.

Systematic problems

Officials also pointed to “serious systemic issues” raised by the case. When police returned the girl to the children’s home that evening, a single night-duty supervisor was responsible for ten children. The institution, they stressed, can only employ a qualified educator alongside supervisory staff during daytime hours.

For years, the system has struggled with single-person night shifts. The home currently has only limited, temporary scope to deploy two staff overnight in severe crisis situations as an exceptional measure.

Magyar government reveals historic modernisation programme of Budapest’s suburban railway system

Further difficulties stem from the increasingly acute mental health conditions of children entering care. A shortage of specialists, inadequate pay, and the regular aggression directed at staff by residents all place significant strain on daily operations, the statement said.

This is compounded by a severe lack of places, particularly for children with special needs, alongside a growing administrative burden and increasingly complex bureaucratic procedures, the Directorate-General added in its response to MTI.

World.title: Romanian authorities mull new dynamic excise duty mechanism to curb fuel prices
World.content:
The Economic Committee, part of Romania’s upper legislative chamber, adopted a favorable report for the draft law on measures to reduce fuel prices on Monday, July 27.

The bill must also receive the approval of the Senate plenary in order to continue its legislative process. If adopted, it will introduce, for the first time, a "dynamic excise duty" mechanism, under which the excise duty on fuel may be reduced by between 5% and 25%, depending on developments in pump prices.

The new version of the bill abandons the VAT reduction initially proposed and retains only the excise duty reduction mechanism, after the Ministry of Finance warned that a VAT cut would not have been compatible with European legislation and would have sent a negative signal to rating agencies.

Former energy minister Bogdan Ivan said the bill creates the legal framework for government intervention during crises on the fuel market through the progressive reduction of the excise duty on diesel.

"At the current pump price of diesel, we are talking about a reduction of RON 0.34 per liter of diesel. If we see an increase in international diesel and oil prices, the reduction could go to as much as RON 0.68, depending on the final price," Bogdan Ivan said, cited by Digi24.

According to him, the purpose of the measure is to keep the price of standard diesel around the threshold of RON 10 per liter, even in the event of further price increases on the international market. The measures are to be applied initially for a period of three months, with the possibility of extension by government decision.

In addition, the Ministry of Finance will be able to update the level of the excise duty once every two weeks, depending on developments in Brent and Platts international quotations.

"Dynamic excise duty means that, depending on the price increase, it can decrease by between 5% and 25%. It is a much more flexible option, which gives us the possibility to act during the three months following promulgation through a Government decision, and every two weeks the Ministry of Finance will analyze the level of the excise duty and take action," interim finance minister Alexandru Nazare said.

He explained that the VAT reduction was dropped because the measure was not compatible with European legislation and would have affected the assessments Romania is expecting in the coming period from the rating agencies.

"We are expecting Fitch's report this week and Moody's report next week, and such announcements regarding VAT reductions would not have helped us at all in maintaining the rating," the minister added.

Nazare specified that the mechanism will be applied for a period of three months, with the possibility of extension, and that the budgetary impact is estimated at approximately RON 100 million per month, depending on price developments. At the same time, he warned that any price-capping measure also involves supply risks, which is why the authorities are in permanent contact with operators in the sector.

World.title: France’s Reed Capital acquires high-precision metal components factory in central Romania
World.content:
French investment fund Reed Capital has acquired Walor Precision Turning, a manufacturer of high-precision metal components for the automotive industry that also operates a factory in Sfântu Gheorghe, central Romania.

Overall, the company has nearly 420 employees and three production facilities in France, Romania, and Mexico. The factory in Sfântu Gheorghe is one of the group's most important assets and supplies major automotive manufacturers, producing high-precision components for airbags and seatbelt pretensioners. According to the company, its products are found in nearly one out of every two cars sold worldwide.

The Romanian subsidiary ended 2025 with a turnover of RON 207.3 million (approximately EUR 40 million), up from RON 202.6 million in 2024. The company returned to profit, reporting a net result of nearly RON 8 million, after a loss of RON 2.8 million recorded the previous year, and had an average of 183 employees.

The acquisition follows the separation of Walor Precision Turning from Walor International, a company previously controlled by the German group Ferral United. Reed Capital said it will retain the current management team and finance investments to expand industrial capacity and diversify the portfolio.

In addition to production meant for the automotive industry, the company wants to expand more strongly into growing industrial markets. The strategy includes developing components for active and semi-active suspension systems, solenoid valves, and, above all, cooling solutions for data centers, a segment driven by massive investments in artificial intelligence and cloud infrastructure.

At the same time, Reed Capital intends to accelerate the company's development in Asia, with a focus on the Chinese market.

"Our ambition is to accelerate the company's diversification toward new industrial applications, particularly cooling solutions for data centers, while at the same time strengthening its international presence, especially in Asia," said Renaud Delaage, managing partner of Reed Capital.

(Photo source: Walor press release)

World.title: Western Romania: Music, culture and sports at Timișoara City Celebration this weekend
World.content:
Timișoara is gearing up for four days of concerts, cultural experiences, sports, heritage and community activities as it holds its City Celebration from July 31 to August 3.

The celebration will bring 203 free events held in the Civic Park, I.C. Brătianu Park and Boulevard, the Uszoda area, Nicolae Titulescu Riverside Promenade, Victory Square and more than 30 other venues throughout the city, the organizers said.

Held under the theme "One city. A thousand ways to experience it," this year's edition “celebrates the communities, cultures, generations and forms of expression that shape contemporary Timișoara.” The music program will bring American singer-songwriter Beth Hart, Irish band The Script, and Serbian singer Marija Šerifović, a 2007 Eurovision winner, to the city.

Alongside the international headliners, the program will feature established local artists and emerging performers from Romania and the Republic of Moldova, including Irina Rimes, Satoshi, Dora Gaitanovici, Alexandra Căpitănescu, JazzyBIT & K-lu by Monica Anghel, Nico, Daniel Iordăchioaie, the folk ensemble Ansamblul Timișul, and Andreea Voica, Alexandru Brădățan, Aurora, and Săndel Mihai.

Timișoara City Celebration will also bring together artists, festivals, and organizations active in the city throughout the year. In the Civic Park and I.C. Brătianu Park, Psihodrom, Muzicon Hub, Time to Rock by FITT, CODRU, Guilty Corner, AnonimTM, Embargo Hub and JAZZx will host concerts, showcases and community-focused events.

From July 31 to August 2, the Uszoda area and the Nicolae Titulescu Riverside Promenade will become a hub for outdoor sports and recreation, featuring competitions, demonstrations and activities for all ages. The program includes 3x3 basketball, rugby and handball tournaments, skateboarding, BMX and scooter competitions, and other activities.

On the evenings of August 1 and August 2, the city’s Victory Square will host Meraviglia | Dancing Fountains, Flames and Aerial Acrobatics, a production combining water, fire, light, music, video projections and aerial performance.

World.title: Car rental company Autonom lists bonds worth EUR 30 mln on Bucharest Stock Exchange
World.content:
Autonom, one of the largest independent Romanian companies in the mobility solutions market, listed its third sustainability-linked bond issue, worth a total of EUR 30 million, on the Main Market of the Bucharest Stock Exchange, or BVB, on Monday, July 27.

The bond issue listed under the ticker AUT31E is made up of 300 bonds with a nominal value of EUR 100,000 each, with a fixed interest rate of 5.97% payable annually. The bonds, set to mature in 2031, are unsecured. Nine institutional investors subscribed to the bond offer.

The funds will be used to achieve the sustainability objectives set out in the company's development strategy.

The bond issuance is structured under the Sustainability-Linked Financing Framework, as the company continues to integrate ESG criteria into its growth strategy. Key ESG performance indicators tracked by Autonom include carbon emissions reduction and gender equality performance. The company aims to reduce the average carbon emissions of its operational passenger car fleet by 30% by 2028 and by 55% by 2030. Moreover, it aims to increase the share of women in management positions to 46% by 2030.

“The fact that the offer was oversubscribed highlights the growing investor interest in sustainable businesses. I congratulate the Autonom team for the consistency and clarity with which they pursue their goals. BVB remains a long-term partner and a steadfast supporter of the company's evolution," stated Remus Vulpescu, CEO of the Bucharest Stock Exchange.

“This new listing confirms that a Romanian entrepreneurial company can repeatedly rely on the capital market to meet its financing needs and integrate sustainability targets into its growth strategy. We would like to thank our investors for their trust and all the partners involved in this new successful listing,” stated Marius and Dan Ștefan, Co-Founders of Autonom.

The listing of the bond issue was carried out with the support of the consortium consisting of BRD – Groupe Société Générale, Banca Comercială Română, BT Capital Partners, Raiffeisen Bank, and UniCredit Bank as Co-Arrangers. Additionally, BRD – Groupe Société Générale represented Autonom for the admission to trading of the AUT31E bonds on the BVB Regulated Market.

Since 2021, Autonom has listed three consecutive sustainability-linked bond issues. The previous bond, AUT26E, valued at EUR 48 million and listed in 202, remains to this day the largest bond issuance by a Romanian entrepreneurial company on the local capital market, maturing in November this year. The third issuance, AUT29E, worth EUR 30 million, will mature in 2029. Before these listings, in 2019, Autonom listed its first bond issue, AUT24E, worth EUR 20 million, which was fully redeemed at maturity.

Autonom is a company with 100% Romanian capital, started in 2006 in Piatra Neamț, and is a top 3 player, by turnover, in the main sectors of activity: operational leasing and car rentals. The company offers modern mobility and financing solutions, including short- and medium-term rentals, operational leasing, chauffeur-driven transfers, temporary fleet rentals, fleet management services, roadside assistance, car wash services, and equipment rentals.

(Photo source: Autonom on Facebook)

World.title: Head of Romania’s Department for Emergency Situations says prosecutor abused powers in alleged fictitious employment case
World.content:
The head of Romania's Department for Emergency Situations (DSU), Raed Arafat, claimed in a video posted on Facebook that the case concerning fictitious employment contracts at the institution he heads was fabricated.

The DSU head said that official checks "confirmed that the prosecutor artificially established jurisdiction in the case by invoking a fabricated factual circumstance." The discovery “dismantles the foundation on which the entire case was built,” Arafat argued.

According to him, based on these "artificial premises," the prosecutor conducted investigations for more than a year without the targeted persons being informed and without them being able to exercise their procedural rights.

At the same time, Arafat added, "the same allegations" were used to obtain "authorization for technical surveillance measures with the highest degree of intrusion." The surveillance lasted 5 months.

"The escalation of the measures did not stop there. The prosecutor also requested authorization for house searches against the investigated persons. However, the judge at the Court of Appeal found these requests to be manifestly disproportionate and rejected them. Instead of accepting the legality review exercised by the court, the prosecutor ordered the forcible seizure of the mobile phones belonging to all 13 targeted persons, obtaining by another route what the court had refused to authorize," Arafat explained.

The DSU chief said that considerable human, logistical, and financial resources were consumed to support a case built on fabricated premises, instead of being directed toward combating real criminal acts.

On March 27, prosecutors conducted searches at the headquarters of the Department for Emergency Situations (DSU) in a case reportedly involving fictitious employment. Subsequently, Raed Arafat "categorically" denied the existence of any possible fictitious employment of doctors within the institution and announced that he had cooperated and would continue to cooperate with investigators.

According to Arafat, the case concerns four doctors and one nurse, all "with extensive experience," employed part-time at the DSU, whom the prosecutor claims were paid without performing the work for which they had been hired. To counter the claims, DSU representatives sent the Military Prosecutor's Office "44 binders containing 20,000 pages demonstrating that the attendance records showed they worked both remotely and physically," and nearly 8,000 pages demonstrating that the people delivered materials, that they worked, and communicated by email, including at midnight."

"In no way can we speak of fraud or fictitious work, as has been claimed," Arafat also said.

Arafat is also included in another case handled by the military section of the National Anticorruption Directorate (DNA) in connection with the 2017 purchase of a helicopter for EUR 4 million, for which VAT allegedly had not been paid. The alleged damage is estimated at approximately EUR 1 million. The DSU head denied any wrongdoing.

World.title: Mortgage-financed home purchases account for over half of Romania's residential transactions
World.content:
More than half of Romania's residential property transactions are now financed through mortgage loans, with the share rising significantly over the past four years, according to an analysis by online mortgage broker Ipotecare.ro based on official data. Nationally, mortgage-backed purchases accounted for just over 57% of residential transactions in the first half of 2026.

In the Bucharest-Ilfov region, mortgages represented almost 59% of residential sales in the first six months of 2026, down slightly from nearly 63% in the same period of 2025, but well above the 50% recorded in 2022, according to calculations based on data from the National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration (ANCPI).

At the national level, the share of residential transactions completed through mortgage financing remained broadly unchanged from last year at just over 57%, compared with 43.5% in 2022, reflecting a stronger increase than in the Bucharest-Ilfov region.

According to the analysis, the nationwide increase in mortgage-financed purchases has coincided with rising home prices in recent years, making it more difficult for buyers to accumulate the funds needed for cash purchases.

The broker also noted that the number of registered mortgages includes refinancing loans. However, refinancings represented only 16% of the loans brokered by Ipotecare.ro this year, with the remaining 84% used to finance home purchases.

“The share of residential transactions completed through mortgage lending has increased and will continue to grow as young people from Generation Z become the main active economic force in the property market. […] The steady fall in mortgage interest rates and the launch of attractive products have also increased interest in mortgage lending," said Laurențiu Bogdan, managing partner at Ipotecare.ro.

The number of homes sold in Bucharest and Ilfov in the first half of 2026 was 1.4% lower than in the same period of last year, while residential sales nationwide declined by nearly 9%, according to ANCPI data.

World.title: Central Romania: Bear chased for two hours through Sibiu’s central neighborhoods
World.content:
A bear was tranquilized and captured by specialized teams on Monday, July 27, after a two-hour chase through central areas of the city of Sibiu. The animal and intervention teams ran through several neighborhoods until the former was cornered, according to local news outlet Turnul Sfatului.

The first alert regarding the presence of the bear was issued at 4:55 AM, when a 112 emergency call reported the presence of the wild animal on General Vasile Milea Boulevard. The authorities immediately issued a warning message, recommending that residents remain indoors and avoid any contact with the animal.

The bear quickly crossed the central area and headed toward the Hipodrom neighborhood. Around 05:20 AM, it entered the courtyard of the "Andrei Șaguna" Pedagogical College. For more than an hour, the animal was monitored by Gendarmerie and SMURD crews while it desperately tried to find a way out, even attempting to dig under the school's fence.

Although a hunter was also present at the scene, prepared to neutralize the bear by shooting it if public safety had been directly threatened, the authorities decided to first attempt immobilization by tranquilization. After several attempts, the intervention team managed to secure the area and administer the tranquilizer.

At 06:45 AM, Sibiu City Hall announced that the mission had been completed, with the animal immobilized without any casualties or major material damage. The bear will be relocated to a mountain area.

Romania is home to a large population of brown bears. According to preliminary results from an April 2025 study by the Ministry of Environment, the country’s brown bear population is estimated at between 10,419 and 12,770 animals. In this context, bear sightings are not uncommon in mountain areas in Romania, even near major cities.

World.title: Romanian worker dies after being struck by beam at Barcelona’s Camp Nou stadium
World.content:
A Romanian worker died after being struck in the head by a beam while carrying out painting work on a platform at the construction site of Barcelona's famed stadium Camp Nou.

Rescue crews confirmed the death of the 54-year-old man. His death was the first fatality registered at Camp Nou, Barcelona's legendary stadium, which has been undergoing modernization works since 2023. An investigation has been opened after the death.

"FC Barcelona deeply regrets the death of the worker who lost his life yesterday in the workplace accident that occurred during the renovation works at Spotify Camp Nou. The Club wishes to express its deepest condolences and extend its heartfelt support to his family, friends, and colleagues. FC Barcelona President Joan Laporta wishes to personally convey his condolences to the family and places himself at their disposal on behalf of the entire Club," the Catalan club said in a statement posted on X.

The Camp Nou construction site is staffed mainly by Romanian and Albanian workers, according to sources cited by TVRInfo.

Set to be fully renovated by 2028, the stadium already hosts matches by Barcelona’s world-famous football team. Once complete, the stadium will be able to accommodate more than 100,000 spectators in the stands.
